dervis-irab:10-11.t:
* I'rab:
(وَما جَعَلَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بُشْرى): the wāw is resumptive, or conjunctive joining to what preceded; ما is negating; جعله الله is a verb, its mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and its fāʿil (agent); the pronoun refers back to the reinforcement (al-imdād); إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); بشرى is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), excepted from the most general of causes. (وَلِتَطْمَئِنَّ بِهِ قُلُوبُكُمْ): the wāw is conjunctive; the lām is causal (li-l-taʿlīl); تطمئن is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an أن implied after it; the preposition and its genitive noun are conjoined to بشرى. The object of purpose is put in the genitive with the lām here because a condition for the accusative is missing, namely identity of the agent; قلوبكم is the fāʿil of تطمئنّ. (وَمَا النَّصْرُ إِلَّا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ): the wāw is resumptive, or also circumstantial; ما is negating; النصر is a mubtadaʾ (subject); إلا is a particle of restriction; من عند الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate). (إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ): the nominal clause gives the reason for what preceded. (إِذْ يُغَشِّيكُمُ النُّعاسَ أَمَنَةً مِنْهُ): إذ is an adverb, a badal (substitute) for إذ يعدكم; it is the second badal, as mentioned before. The clause يغشيكم النعاس is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); النعاس is a mafʿūl bihi; أمنة is a ḥāl (circumstantial) or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi; منه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of أمنة. (وَيُنَزِّلُ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ بِهِ): ينزل is conjoined to يغشيكم; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ينزل, and likewise من السماء; ماء is a mafʿūl bihi; ليطهركم: the lām is causal and يطهركم is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an أن implied after it; به is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يطهركم. (وَيُذْهِبَ عَنْكُمْ رِجْزَ الشَّيْطانِ وَلِيَرْبِطَ عَلى قُلُوبِكُمْ وَيُثَبِّتَ بِهِ الْأَقْدامَ): clauses conjoined to what preceded. The pronoun in به refers to the water, so that walking on the sand becomes easy, since walking on it is usually difficult, but when water falls on it, it becomes firm and walking on it becomes easy. It is also said that the pronoun refers to the strengthening (al-rabṭ), because when patience and boldness are firmly established in the heart, the feet are made firm in the places of battle.

dervis-irab:12-14.t:
* Vocabulary:
(البنان): the fingers, as in al-Miṣbāḥ, or their tips; the singular is بنانة.
Abū al-Haytham said: البنان means the joints, and every joint is a بنانة. It is also said: البنان means the fingers of the hands and the feet, and all the joints of every limb.
(شاقُّوا) [Translator's note: the opening of this headword is damaged in the source text («َاقُّوا)»); it is the word شاقّوا of the ayah.]: they opposed. المشاقّة is derived from الشقّ (side, split), because each of two enemies is on a side (ʿudwa) other than the side of his fellow; and likewise المخاصمة, because this one is in one خصم, i.e. on one side, and that one in another خصم.

* I'rab:
(إِذْ يُوحِي رَبُّكَ إِلَى الْمَلائِكَةِ أَنِّي مَعَكُمْ): the adverb may be a third badal (substitute) for إذ يعدكم; it may also be in the accusative governed by يثبت, or be governed by an omitted verb, i.e. «اذكر» (remember). The clause يوحي ربك is in the position of a genitive by annexation; إلى الملائكة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يوحي; أني together with what falls in its scope is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of يوحي; معكم is an adverb attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of أني. (فَثَبِّتُوا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that reveals an omitted condition), i.e. if this is established, then make firm those who believe by giving them glad tidings of victory; الذين is a mafʿūl bihi, and the clause آمنوا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. (سَأُلْقِي فِي قُلُوبِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الرُّعْبَ):
the clause may be an explanation of His saying:
إني معكم فثبتوا, for there is no help more emphatic and more effective than casting terror into the hearts of the enemies; or it may be resumptive. In both cases it has no grammatical position. في قلوب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ألقي; الرعب is the mafʿūl bihi of ألقي; the clause كفروا has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun. (فَاضْرِبُوا فَوْقَ الْأَعْناقِ وَاضْرِبُوا مِنْهُمْ كُلَّ بَنانٍ): an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); فوق is an adverb attached to اضربوا, and the mafʿūl bihi is omitted, i.e. "so strike them above the necks". «فوق» may also be a mafʿūl bihi by extension of usage (ʿalā al-ittisāʿ), because it denotes the head.
It is as if it were said: "so strike above their heads", and this is what al-Zamakhsharī chose. He said:
«He meant the upper parts of the necks, which are the places of slaughter, because they are joints, so that a blow landing there would be a cutting through and a sending of heads flying. And it is said: He meant the heads, because they are above the necks, meaning a striking of the skulls. ʿAmr ibn al-Iṭnāba said:
أبت لي عفّتي وأبى بلائي ... وأخذي الحمد بالثمن الربيح
وإقدامي على المكروه نفسي ... وضربي هامة البطل المشيح
لأدفع عن مآثر صالحات ... وأحجب بعد عن عرض صحيح
(Gloss: My chastity refused it for me, and my prowess, and my winning praise at a profitable price, and my pressing my own self forward into what is hateful, and my striking the skull of the wary champion — so that I might defend noble deeds of glory and then shield a sound honour.)
[Translator's note: the source has «لأن نها» in this quotation, evidently a misprint for «لأنها» (because they are); translated accordingly. The source also does not mark where al-Zamakhsharī's quotation ends.]
(ذلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ شَاقُّوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ) [Translator's note: the opening of this ayah segment is damaged in the source («لِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ…»).]:
the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the reference is to what befell them of striking, killing and punishment; بأنهم is its khabar; the clause شاقّوا الله ورسوله is the khabar of أنّ; the Name of Majesty (Allah) is a mafʿūl bihi, and رسوله is conjoined to it.
(وَمَنْ يُشاقِقِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ) [Translator's note: the opening of this ayah segment is also damaged in the source («َ مَنْ يُشاقِقِ…»).]:
the wāw is resumptive; من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; يشاقون [Translator's note: so in the source; the word in the ayah is يشاقق] is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa); إنّ, its noun and its khabar [form the apodosis]; the protasis and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) are the khabar of «من». The conditional sentence here is a completion of what came before it and a repetition of its content. (ذلِكُمْ فَذُوقُوهُ وَأَنَّ لِلْكافِرِينَ عَذابَ النَّارِ): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ; the address is to the disbelievers by way of iltifāt (sudden shift of address); the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "the punishment". You may also parse the demonstrative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e.:
"the punishment is that"; it may also be in the position of an accusative by ishtighāl (a noun whose verb is occupied with its pronoun), as when you say:
زيدا فاضربه ("Zayd — strike him"). In every case the fāʾ is resumptive and ذوقوه is a resumptive statement. أنّ is conjoined to ذلكم under all three of its analyses; للكافرين is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar of «أنّ», placed first; عذاب النار is its noun, placed after. The meaning is: taste this immediate punishment together with the deferred one.

* Rhetoric:
In these ayat there are numerous devices of rhetoric, to which we alluded during the i'rab because of their connection with it: majāz (figurative usage), iltifāt (shift of address), and istiʿāra (metaphor) in His saying «فذقوه» [Translator's note: so in the source; the ayah reads فذوقوه]. These devices have been discussed before in their places.

dervis-irab:15-18.t:
* Vocabulary:
(زَحْفاً): الزحف is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of زحف. In al-Miṣbāḥ: زحف القوم زحفا (the people advanced), of the pattern of نفع, and also زحوفا. A large army is called زحف, naming it by the maṣdar; the plural is زحوف, like فلس and فلوس. And a child زحف on the ground (crawls) before he walks.
(مُتَحَرِّفاً): turning aside; or it is attacking again after retreating, so as to make the enemy imagine that one has been routed, then turning back on him. It is one of the ruses and stratagems of war.
(مُتَحَيِّزاً): withdrawing to join, gathering oneself to. التحيّز and التحوّز mean joining up (al-inḍimām); تحوّزت الحية: the snake coiled itself up; حزت الشيء: I gathered the thing to me; الحوزة is what gathers things together. The original form of متحيّز is متحيوز: the yāʾ and the wāw came together, the first of them being vowelless, so the wāw was changed into a yāʾ and the yāʾ was assimilated into the yāʾ.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): its i'rab has been given many times before. (إِذا لَقِيتُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا زَحْفاً فَلا تُوَلُّوهُمُ الْأَدْبارَ): إذا is an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition; the clause لقيتم is in the position of a genitive by annexation; الذين is its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause); زحفا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الذين, i.e. while they are advancing. It is also said: «زحفا» is in the accusative as a maṣdar governed by an omitted ḥāl, i.e. زاحفين زحفا (advancing an advance). This that has been said is muḥkam [i.e. firmly established, not abrogated], so fleeing at the encounter is forbidden in every case. The fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa); لا is prohibitive; تولوهم is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by لا; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi, and الأدبار is a second mafʿūl bihi. (وَمَنْ يُوَلِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ دُبُرَهُ):
the wāw is resumptive; من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ (subject); يولهم is a verb, its latent (mustatir) agent and its first object; دبره is the second object of يولهم; يومئذ is an adverb annexed to an adverb, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يولهم. (إِلَّا مُتَحَرِّفاً لِقِتالٍ أَوْ مُتَحَيِّزاً إِلى فِئَةٍ): «إلا» may be a particle of restriction because of the preceding prohibition, and متحرفا is a ḥāl; or «إلا» may be a particle of exception, and متحرفا is excepted from the pronoun of the believers. لقتال is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «متحرفا»; أو متحيزا إلى فئة is conjoined to what precedes it. (فَقَدْ باءَ بِغَضَبٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ): the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) because the apodosis is joined with قد; باء is a past verb; بغضب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to باء or to an omitted ḥāl; من الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective); the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis. (وَمَأْواهُ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ): the wāw is resumptive or conjunctive; مأواه is a mubtadaʾ and جهنم its khabar (predicate); بئس is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; المصير is the fāʿil of بئس; the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. "their destination". (فَلَمْ تَقْتُلُوهُمْ وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ قَتَلَهُمْ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (revealing an omitted condition), i.e. if you boast of having killed them, [know that] you did not kill them; so it has come as the apodosis of an implied condition. لم is a particle of negation, of conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning] and of the jussive; تقتلوهم is an imperfect verb in the jussive by لم. The wāw is a conjunction; لكنّ is a particle resembling the verb (one of the sisters of inna), and it has come in the best of ways, since it falls between a negation and an affirmation; الله is its noun and the clause قتلهم is its khabar. (وَما رَمَيْتَ إِذْ رَمَيْتَ وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ رَمى): conjoined to what preceded; إذ is an adverb of past time attached to رميت; the wāw is conjunctive; لكنّ and its noun, and the clause رمى is its khabar. (وَلِيُبْلِيَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ مِنْهُ بَلاءً حَسَناً إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ): the wāw is conjunctive; the lām is causal; يبلي is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied أن; أن together with what falls in its scope is in the position of a genitive by the lām, and both are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being:
"He did that". المؤمنين is a mafʿūl bihi; بلاء is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). البلاء here is understood as favour, because it applies to both favour and trial, since its root meaning is testing, and it is reducible to that; حسنا is a naʿt. إن الله سميع عليم is conjoined to what preceded: إنّ, its noun and its two khabars. (ذلِكُمْ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ مُوهِنُ كَيْدِ الْكافِرِينَ): the i'rab of a parallel to the demonstrative has been given before: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "that testing is true"; وأن الله: أنّ together with what falls in its scope is conjoined to ذلكم; موهن is the khabar of «أنّ», and كيد الكافرين is annexed to موهن (muḍāf ilayhi). The reference is to the killing, the throwing and the testing. «أنّ» together with what falls in its scope may also be conjoined to «وليبلي», or be in the position of an accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "and know that Allah…".

* Rhetoric:
1- The device of taʿrīḍ (allusion, innuendo):
In the saying of Allah the Exalted «ومن يولهم يومئذ دبره» there is a device called taʿrīḍ, which some include under kināya (metonymy). al-Saʿd al-Taftāzānī said:
«When a kināya is allusive (ʿaraḍiyya), framed for the sake of a described person who is not mentioned, it is fitting to call it taʿrīḍ. One says: ʿarraḍtu li-fulān and ʿarraḍtu bi-fulān, when you say something while meaning him, as if you pointed to one side (ʿurḍ) while intending another side. From it come al-maʿārīḍ in speech, which is tawriya (double entendre), alluding by one thing to another.» al-Zamakhsharī said: «Kināya is to mention a thing by other than the word coined for it; taʿrīḍ is to mention something by which you indicate something you have not mentioned, as when the needy person says to the one he needs: "I have come to you to greet you". It is as if he inclined the speech towards a side (ʿurḍ) that points to the intended meaning; and the ʿurḍ of a thing, with ḍamma, is its side, from whichever direction you come to it.»
Ibn al-Athīr said in al-Mathal al-Sāʾir: «Kināya is what indicates a meaning that may be taken in the direction of both the literal (ḥaqīqa) and the figurative (majāz) by a quality common to both, and it occurs in single words and in compound expressions. Taʿrīḍ is the expression that indicates a meaning not by way of literal or figurative coinage, but by way of hinting and pointing; so it is specific to compound expressions, as in the saying of one who hopes for a gift: "By Allah, I am in need", for it is an allusive request although it was not coined for that either literally or figuratively; the meaning was understood from it only from the side (ʿurḍ) of the expression, i.e. its flank.»
Once you have understood this, it will be easy for you to recognise the secret of the taʿrīḍ in this elegant expression in the ayah: He mentioned to them a state that is considered shameful in the one who does it, and so He used the word الدبر (the backside) rather than الظهر (the back).
Abū al-Ṭayyib [al-Mutanabbī] was fond of this device. He said, alluding to Kāfūr al-Ikhshīdī:
ومن ركب الثور بعد الجوا ... د أنكر أظلافه والغبب
(Gloss: Whoever rides the ox after the steed finds its hooves and its dewlap strange.)
He means that one who rides the ox, while his habit was to ride the steed, finds the ox's hooves and dewlap strange; but one like Kāfūr, who had ridden the ox before, does not find that strange if he rides it after the steed. He also said, asking Kāfūr for more gifts after praising him:
أبا المسك هل في الكأس فضل أناله ... فإني أغني منذ حين وتشرب
(Gloss: O Abū al-Misk, is there anything left in the cup that I may obtain? For I have been singing for a while, and you drink.)
He is saying: my praise of you delights you as singing delights the drinker, so it is time that you give me to drink from what is left in your cup. Then he said after it:
وهبت على مقدار كفّي زماننا ... ونفسي على مقدار كفّيك تطلب
(Gloss: You have given according to the measure of the palms of our time, while my soul asks according to the measure of your palms.)
2- The device of istidrāk (rectification) and rujūʿ (retraction):
It is speech containing the word «لكن». It is of two kinds: a kind in which the istidrāk is preceded by an affirmation, and a kind in which it is not. Of the second kind is the saying of Allah the Exalted: «فلم تقتلوهم ولكن الله قتلهم، وما رميت إذ رميت ولكن الله رمى». The istidrāk has come in these words in two places, each of which is prepared for taʿaṭṭuf (the turning back of a word upon itself), for the words تقتلوهم and قتلهم, and رميت and رمى, turn back upon each other.
This is the closest istidrāk that has occurred in speech, because its particle stands in the middle between the two words of taʿaṭṭuf in both places. An example of the first kind will come shortly.
Among what has come of it in poetry is the saying of Abū al-Ṭayyib:
هم المحسنون الكرّ في حومة الوغى ... وأحسن منه كرّهم في المكارم
ولولا احتقار الأسد شبّهتها بهم ... لكنّها معدودة في البهائم
(Gloss: They are the ones who excel at charging in the thick of battle, and better still is their charging in noble deeds; were it not for contempt of lions I would have likened them to them, but lions are counted among the beasts.)
And how beautiful is the saying of one of them about a head crucified on a spear:
وعاد لكنّه رأس بلا جسد ... يمشي ولكن على ساق بلا قدم
إذا تراءى على الخطي أسفر في ... حال العبوس لنا عن ثغر مبتسم
(Gloss: He returned, but as a head without a body, walking, but on a shank without a foot; when he appears upon the spear, in the midst of grimness he reveals to us a smiling mouth.)

* Benefits:
History relates that on the day of Uḥud, Ubayy ibn Khalaf began galloping his horse until he came near the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Some of the Muslim men stood in the way of Ubayy ibn Khalaf to kill him, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: "Stand back", so they stood back. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took his short spear in his hand and threw it at Ubayy ibn Khalaf, breaking one of his ribs. Ubayy ibn Khalaf went back to his companions weighed down, and they carried him as they turned back to go home, and they began to say: "No harm." When they said that to him, Ubayy said: "By Allah, had it been on all the people, it would have killed them. Did he not say: I will kill you, if Allah wills?" His companions set off with him, trying to revive him, until he died somewhere on the road and they buried him. Ibn al-Musayyab said: and concerning that Allah revealed:
«وما رميت إذ رميت».

dervis-irab:19-23.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَسْتَفْتِحُوا): you seek the fatḥ, i.e. the judgement and decision between you and Muḥammad, by giving victory to the one in the right and forsaking the one in the wrong. It is related that when they wanted to set out, they clung to the curtains of the Kaʿba and said: "O Allah, whichever of us cut the ties of kinship more and brought us what we do not know, then فأحنه (bring him to ruin) this morning", i.e. destroy him.
(الدَّوَابِّ): the plural of دابّة (creature). What is meant by it here is the human being. Applying دابّة to the human being is literal (ḥaqīqī), because of what they mention in the books of language, namely that it is applied to every animal, even a human. In al-Miṣbāḥ: الدابة is every living creature on the earth, whether endowed with discernment or not.

* I'rab:
(إِنْ تَسْتَفْتِحُوا فَقَدْ جاءَكُمُ الْفَتْحُ): إن is conditional; تستفتحوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa) because the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is joined with قد; قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); جاءكم الفتح is a verb, its mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and its fāʿil (agent). (وَإِنْ تَنْتَهُوا فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ): conjoined to what preceded, and the i'rab is like what came before it. The apodosis is joined with the fāʾ because it is a nominal clause composed of a mubtadaʾ (subject) and a khabar (predicate). The apodosis clause in both places is in the position of a jussive. (وَإِنْ تَعُودُوا نَعُدْ): also conjoined.
The apodosis clause has no grammatical position. (وَلَنْ تُغْنِيَ عَنْكُمْ فِئَتُكُمْ شَيْئاً وَلَوْ كَثُرَتْ): also conjoined; فئتكم is the fāʿil of تغني; شيئا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or a mafʿūl bihi; the wāw is circumstantial; لو is conditional; كثرت is the protasis, and the apodosis is omitted.
(وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): also conjoined. The hamza of «أنّ» takes fatḥa by implying the lām; the implied form is ولأنّ الله مع المؤمنين (and because Allah is with the believers). الله is the noun of أنّ, and مع is an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted word which is the khabar. (يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): its i'rab has been given before. (أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَلا تَوَلَّوْا عَنْهُ وَأَنْتُمْ تَسْمَعُونَ): أطيعوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil; الله is a mafʿūl bihi and رسوله is conjoined to الله; the clause ولا تولوا is conjoined to the clause أطيعوا; لا is prohibitive; تولوا is an imperfect in the jussive by the prohibitive لا, the wāw being the fāʿil; عنه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تولوا; وأنتم: the wāw is circumstantial, أنتم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause تسمعون is the khabar. (وَلا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ قالُوا سَمِعْنا وَهُمْ لا يَسْمَعُونَ): conjoined to what preceded. The kāf is a noun meaning مثل (like), the khabar of تكونوا; and it is a preposition, the preposition and its genitive noun being the khabar [Translator's note: the source gives both analyses side by side in this way, presumably as alternatives]. The clause قالوا is the ṣila (relative clause); the clause سمعنا is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl); the wāw is circumstantial, and the clause هم لا يسمعون is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(إِنَّ شَرَّ الدَّوَابِّ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الصُّمُّ الْبُكْمُ الَّذِينَ لا يَعْقِلُونَ): إنّ and its noun; عند الله: the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl; الصم is the khabar of إنّ, البكم a second khabar; الذين is a naʿt (adjective), and the clause لا يعقلون is the ṣila. (وَلَوْ عَلِمَ اللَّهُ فِيهِمْ خَيْراً لَأَسْمَعَهُمْ): the wāw is resumptive; لو is a particle of non-occurrence because of non-occurrence (imtināʿ li-mtināʿ), containing the sense of a condition; علم الله is a verb and its fāʿil; فيهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to علم; خيرا is a mafʿūl bihi; لأسمعهم: the lām links the apodosis of لو, and أسمعهم is a verb with its latent (mustatir) agent, the hāʾ being a mafʿūl bihi. (وَلَوْ أَسْمَعَهُمْ لَتَوَلَّوْا وَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ): the wāw is conjunctive; لو is merely for linking and cannot be the لو of non-occurrence, because the meaning would then become: their turning away did not occur because their being made to hear did not occur, and this is contrary to fact. So here it is merely for linking, in the sense of إن. أسمعهم is a past verb and the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi; لتولوا: the lām is linking, and تولوا is a past verb and its fāʿil; the wāw is circumstantial; هم معرضون is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl. The difference between the two "makings to hear" is that by the first is meant: if Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear with a hearing through which He creates guidance and acceptance for them; and [by the second]: if He had made them hear — not in the sense that He creates guidance for them, but a bare hearing devoid of that — they would have turned away, averse.

* Benefits:
Ibn Hishām said:
«Students have been persistently asking about the saying of Allah the Exalted: «ولو علم الله فيهم خيرا لأسمعهم ولو أسمعهم لتولوا». The point of it is that a syllogism (qiyās) can be composed from the two clauses, and it would then yield: "If Allah had known any good in them, they would have turned away", and this is impossible.
The answer is from three angles. Two come back to denying that it is a syllogism, by establishing that the middle term differs. The first of them is that the implied sense is: "He would have made them hear with a beneficial hearing; and if He had made them hear [any] hearing, they would have turned away." The second is to imply: "And if He had made them hear", on the supposition that He had not known any good in them. The third is on the supposition that it is a syllogism with a unified middle term and a valid conclusion, the implied sense being: "If Allah had known good in him at some time, they would have turned away after that time."
[Translator's note: the source does not mark where Ibn Hishām's quotation ends.]

dervis-irab:24-26.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): its i'rab has been given before. (اسْتَجِيبُوا لِلَّهِ وَلِلرَّسُولِ إِذا دَعاكُمْ لِما يُحْيِيكُمْ): استجيبوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); لله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) استجيبوا; للرسول is conjoined to لله; إذا is a future adverb; the clause دعاكم is in the position of a genitive by annexation; لما is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to دعاكم; the clause يحييكم is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. They differed over His saying «لما يحييكم»; the soundest view is that it is general, covering everything in which there is life for the hearts, salvation and protection in this world and the Hereafter. (وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَقَلْبِهِ): اعلموا is conjoined to استجيبوا; أنّ together with what falls in its scope stands in place of the two objects of اعلموا; the clause يحول is the khabar (predicate) of أنّ; بين is an adverb attached to يحول; المرء is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and قلبه is conjoined to المرء. The meaning of the majāz (figurative usage) in Allah's coming between a man and his heart will come in the section on rhetoric. (وَأَنَّهُ إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ): conjoined to أنّ الله; إليه is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تحشرون; the clause تحشرون is the khabar of أنّ. (وَاتَّقُوا فِتْنَةً لا تُصِيبَنَّ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْكُمْ خَاصَّةً): اتقوا is conjoined to استجيبوا and اعلموا; فتنة is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause لا تصيبن is a naʿt (adjective) of فتنة, and «لا» on this view is negating. It may also be governed by an omitted verb of saying, لا then being prohibitive, and that saying is the naʿt, i.e. "a trial about which it is said: let it not befall…". The prohibition in form is addressed to the trial, and in meaning to those addressed. al-Zamakhsharī parsed it beautifully, saying, in his exact words: «His saying «لا تصيبن» must be either the response to the command, or a prohibition after a command, or a naʿt of فتنة. If it is a response, the meaning is: if it befalls you, it will not befall only the wrongdoers among you, but it will encompass you all.
This is like what is related, that the scholars of the Children of Israel forbade evil only half-heartedly (taʿdhīran), so Allah enveloped them in punishment. If it is a prohibition after a command, it is as if it were said: beware of a sin or a punishment; then it was said: do not expose yourselves to wrongdoing, lest the punishment, or the effect and evil consequence of the sin, befall specifically those of you who did wrong. And likewise if you make it a naʿt with a verb of saying intended, as if it were said: and beware of a trial about which it is said: let it not befall… Its parallel is the saying [of the poet]:
حتى إذا جنّ الظلام واختلط ... جاءوا بمذق هل رأيت الذئب قطّ
(Gloss: Until, when darkness fell and mingled, they brought watered-down milk [of the kind of which one says]: "Have you ever seen the wolf?")»
[Translator's note: the source does not mark where al-Zamakhsharī's quotation ends; the closing mark here is placed before the author resumes his parsing.]
الذين is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause ظلموا is the ṣila; منكم is a ḥāl (circumstantial); خاصة is in the accusative as a ḥāl from the latent (mustatir) agent in His saying لا تصيبن. Its origin is to be a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being: إصابة خاصة (a specific befalling). (وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ): أنّ together with what falls in its scope stands in place of the two objects of اعلموا. (وَاذْكُرُوا إِذْ أَنْتُمْ قَلِيلٌ مُسْتَضْعَفُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ): اذكروا is conjoined to اعلموا; إذ: the adverb is in the accusative here as a mafʿūl bihi, not as an adverb, i.e. remember the time when you were few and oppressed; the clause أنتم قليل is annexed to the adverb; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) of which three khabars are predicated: قليل, مستضعفون and في الأرض. (تَخافُونَ أَنْ يَتَخَطَّفَكُمُ النَّاسُ): the clause تخافون is a naʿt like the one before it, i.e. "fearing"; it may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «قليل» and «مستضعفون». أن together with what falls in its scope is the mafʿūl bihi of تخافون, and الناس is the fāʿil of يتخطفكم. (فَآواكُمْ وَأَيَّدَكُمْ بِنَصْرِهِ وَرَزَقَكُمْ مِنَ الطَّيِّباتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ): the fāʾ is conjunctive; آواكم is a past verb with a latent agent, and what follows is conjoined to it; لعلّ and its noun, and the clause تشكرون is its khabar.

* Benefits:
Ibn Hishām said in al-Mughnī, in these words: «The saying of Allah the Exalted: «لا تصيبن الذين ظلموا منكم خاصة»: لا may be taken as prohibitive or as negating. On the first, it is the content of an omitted verb of saying, which is the naʿt, i.e. "a trial about which that is said"; this is supported by the fact that emphasising the verb with the nūn after the prohibitive لا is regular (qiyās), as in:
«ولا تحسبن الله غافلا». On the second, it is a naʿt of فتنة; this is supported by its being free of implying [an omitted verb of saying]. The second condition is its being fit to be dispensed with; by this are excluded the ṣila, the khabar clause, and the clause quoted by a verb of saying, for these cannot be dispensed with, in the sense that the intelligibility of the saying depends on them.
[Translator's note: this passage is compressed or garbled in the source («ويرجحه سلامته من تقدير القيد الثاني صلاحيتها للاستغناء عنها»); it is translated as it can best be read, and the source does not mark where the quotation ends.]
Abū Ḥayyān said: «The clause in His saying «لا تصيبن» is declarative, a naʿt of His saying «فتنة», i.e. not befalling the wrongdoer specifically. However, the entry of the emphatic nūn on a verb negated by «لا» is disputed: the majority do not allow it, and they take what has occurred of it as poetic licence or rarity. What we choose is that it is permissible, and some grammarians have held this view. Since its attaching to a verb negated by «لا» has occurred even with separation, as in the saying [of the poet]:
فلا ذا نعيم يتركن لنعيمه ... وإن قال قرّظني وخذ رشوة أبى
ولا ذا بئيس يتركنّ لبؤسه ... فينفعه شكوى إليه إن اشتكى
(Gloss: He does not leave a man of comfort alone for his comfort — even if he says "Praise me and take a bribe", he refuses — nor does he leave a wretched man alone for his wretchedness, so that complaining to him might benefit him if he complains.)
then its attaching to it without separation is all the more appropriate, as in: ولا تصيبن.»
[Translator's note: the source does not mark where Abū Ḥayyān's quotation ends.]

* Rhetoric:
1- Majāz (figurative usage) in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «يحول بين المرء وقلبه». The root meaning of الحول is a thing's changing and its separating from something else. In respect of change one says: حال الشيء يحول (the thing changed); and in respect of separation one says: حال بينهما (it came between the two). So the literal sense of Allah's coming between a man and his heart is that He separates them; it is thus a majāz mursal (metonymic trope) for extreme nearness to the servant, because whoever separates two things is nearer to each of them than the other is, since he is in contact with both. The relationship (ʿalāqa) is that of place (al-maḥalliyya) or of causality (al-sababiyya). The speech may also be an istiʿāra tamthīliyya (extended metaphor) for His extreme nearness to the servant and His knowledge of what is hidden in hearts and the secrets of souls.
2- There is disagreement about «لا» in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «واتقوا فتنة لا تصيبن الذين ظلموا منكم خاصة», with two views:
a- That «لا» is prohibitive, and it is a prohibition after a command, i.e. it is speech cut off from what precedes it, as when you say: "Pray the dawn prayer, and do not strike Zayd." The original is: beware of a fitna, i.e. a punishment; then it was said: do not expose yourselves to the fitna lest it befall those who … etc. On this view the befalling is restricted to those who expose themselves. The emphasis of the verb with the nūn is clear, since it is joined with a particle of request, as in «ولا تحسبنّ الله غافلا». But a request cannot occur as a naʿt of an indefinite noun, so a verb of saying must be implied, i.e. "and beware of a trial about which that is said", as has been said concerning the saying [of the poet]: حتى إذا جن الظلام واختلط ... جاءوا بمذق هل رأيت الذئب قط
b- That it is negating. Those who hold this differ in two views. One of them is that the clause is a naʿt of فتنة, and there is no need to imply a verb of saying, since the clause is declarative.
[Translator's note: a passage appears to have dropped out of the source here; the following verse is cited without introduction, evidently as an example of the emphatic nūn after negating لا.]
فلا الجارة الدنيا بها تلحينّها ... ولا الضيف فيها إن أناخ محوّل
(Gloss: Neither will you blame the nearest neighbour-woman in it, nor is the guest in it, if he makes his camel kneel, turned away.)
Indeed, it is easier in the ayah, since there is no separation, and in both it is based on what is heard (samāʿī). What has made it permissible is likening the negating لا to the prohibitive لا. On this view, the befalling is general to the wrongdoer and others, not specific to the wrongdoers, as al-Zamakhsharī mentioned, because it has been described as not befalling the wrongdoers specifically; how then could it, with this, be specific to them! The second is that the verb is the response to the command; on this view too the emphasis is outside the regular rule and anomalous (shādhdh). Among those who mentioned this view is al-Zamakhsharī, and it is unsound, because the meaning would then be: "for if you guard against it, it will not befall the wrongdoer specifically." And his saying that the implied form is:
"if it befalls you, it will not befall the wrongdoer specifically" is rejected, because the condition is only implied from the kind of the command, not from the kind of the response.

dervis-irab:60-61.t:
* Vocabulary:
(رِباطِ الْخَيْلِ): those of them that are tethered; ribāṭ al-khayl is keeping horses tied up and acquiring them. A poet said: فينا رباط جياد الخيل معلمة ... وفي كليب رباط اللؤم والعار (Among us are the tethered, marked thoroughbred horses, while among Kulayb are tethered baseness and disgrace.)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Al-ribāṭ is a name for the horses that are tethered in the way of Allah. It may also be named after al-ribāṭ in the sense of al-murābaṭa (garrisoning the frontier), and it may be the plural of rabīṭ, like faṣīl and fiṣāl. The maṣdar (verbal noun) here is annexed to its object."
In al-Miṣbāḥ: rabaṭahu rabṭan — of the pattern ḍaraba and of the pattern qatala — linguistically means he tied it fast. Al-ribāṭ is that with which the water-skin and the like are tied; its plural is rubuṭ, like kitāb and kutub. Of one afflicted it is said: rabaṭa Allāhu ʿalā qalbihi bi-l-ṣabr (May Allah bind his heart with patience), just as it is said: afragha Allāhu ʿalayhi al-ṣabr, i.e. He inspired him with it. Al-ribāṭ is also a noun from rābaṭa murābaṭatan — of the pattern qātala — when one keeps to the enemy's frontier. The ribāṭ that is built for the poor is a post-classical (muwallad) usage; by analogy its plural is rubuṭ, with two ḍammas, and ribāṭāt. End of quotation. We consider that what accords with "strength", which is shooting, is that al-ribāṭ be taken in its ordinary sense; and Allah knows best.
(جنح) lahu and ilayhi: he inclined. Janaḥat al-ibil: the camels bent their necks. The maṣdar is al-junūḥ. It is said: janaḥa al-layl, the night approached. Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl said: janaḥa al-rajul ilā fulān and li-fulān, when he submits to him. Al-junūḥ also means following, because it includes the sense of inclining. From it come al-jawāniḥ for the ribs, because they bend over a person's insides, and al-janāḥ (the wing), from the same root, because it inclines over the bird. Dhū al-Rumma said:
إذا مات فوق الرحل أحييت روحه ... بذكراك والعيس المراسيل جنح
(When he dies [of weariness] upon the saddle, you revive his spirit by the mention of you, while the swift white camels lean forward [in their pace].)
And al-Nābigha said:
جوانح قد أيقن أن قبيله ... إذا ما التقى الجمعان أول غالب
([Birds] inclining [to follow the army], certain that his tribe, when the two hosts meet, will be the first to prevail.)
(السلم) with kasra or fatḥa on the sīn: peace. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Al-silm, with kasra or fatḥa on the sīn, is reconciliation (al-ṣulḥ); it is treated as masculine and feminine." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Al-salm is made feminine as its opposite, war (al-ḥarb), is feminine." ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās said, addressing Khufāf ibn Nudba:
السلم تأخذ منها ما رضيت به ... والحرب يكفيك من أنفاسها جرع
(From peace you take whatever you are pleased with, while of war a few gulps of its breaths suffice you.)

* I'rab:
(وَأَعِدُّوا لَهُمْ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ مِنْ قُوَّةٍ وَمِنْ رِباطِ الْخَيْلِ): the wāw is a conjunction; أعدوا is an imperative verb and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أعدوا — what is meant is those who break the covenant, as the context of the speech requires, or the disbelievers in general; ما is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause استطعتم is the ṣila (relative clause); من قوة is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the relative noun or of the pronoun referring back to it; and من رباط الخيل is conjoined to it.
(تُرْهِبُونَ بِهِ عَدُوَّ اللَّهِ وَعَدُوَّكُمْ وَآخَرِينَ مِنْ دُونِهِمْ): the clause ترهبون is a ḥāl of the agent of أعدوا, i.e. "while you are striking terror", or a ḥāl of the object of أعدوا, which is the relative noun, i.e. "while it is something by which terror is struck"; به is attached to ترهبون; عدو الله is the object of ترهبون; عدوكم is conjoined to عدو الله; and آخرين is conjoined to عدوكم — what is meant by them is the Jews; من دونهم is a naʿt (adjective) of آخرين.
(لا تَعْلَمُونَهُمُ اللَّهُ يَعْلَمُهُمْ): the clause لا تعلمونهم is an adjective of آخرين; الله is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause يعلمهم is the khabar (predicate); the second object is omitted, its implied form being "fighting [against you]" (muḥāribīn).
(وَما تُنْفِقُوا مِنْ شَيْءٍ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ يُوَفَّ إِلَيْكُمْ وَأَنْتُمْ لا تُظْلَمُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; ما is a conditional noun causing the jussive, in the position of the accusative as an object placed before تنفقوا; تنفقوا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); من شيء is a ḥāl; في سبيل الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to تنفقوا; يوف is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun; إليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يوف; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا تظلمون is the khabar, and the clause is conjoined.
(وَإِنْ جَنَحُوا لِلسَّلْمِ فَاجْنَحْ لَها وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ): the wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; جنحوا is a past verb, and it is the protasis; للسلم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to جنحوا; the fāʾ links [the apodosis]; اجنح is an imperative verb; لها is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to اجنح; توكل is conjoined to اجنح; على الله is attached to توكل; إنّ and its noun; هو is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); السميع is a first khabar and العليم a second khabar. It is also possible that هو is a mubtadaʾ with السميع العليم as its two predicates, the clause being the khabar of إنه.

* Benefits:
A discussion of the feminine
Know that the Arabs have made many nouns feminine by means of an implied (muqaddar) tāʾ. This implied tāʾ is inferred from: the pronoun referring back to them, as in «النار وعدها الله الذين كفروا», «حتى تضع الحرب أوزارها», and «وإن جنحوا للسلم فاجنح لها»; pointing to them, as in «هذه جهنم»; the presence of the tāʾ in their diminutive, as in udhayna and ʿuyayna, diminutives of udhun (ear) and ʿayn (eye), among the paired bodily members — for the diminutive returns things to their origins — whereas the unpaired members are masculine, like al-raʾs (head) and al-qalb (heart); or the presence of the tāʾ in their verb, as in «ولما فصلت العير»; or its absence from their numeral, as in the words of Ḥumayd al-Arqaṭ describing an Arab bow:
أرمي عليها وهي فرع أجمع ... وهي ثلاث أذرع وأصبع
(I shoot with it, and it is all of a single branch; it is three cubits and a finger long.)
Adhruʿ is the plural of dhirāʿ, which is feminine, as shown by the absence of the tāʾ from its numeral, thalāth.
Further, the well-known rule is that whatever of the bodily members is paired is predominantly feminine, except the two eyebrows, the two nostrils and the two cheeks, which are masculine; the final authority is what is heard from the Arabs (al-samāʿ). Counting the two nostrils among the paired does not conflict with counting the nose among the unpaired, because al-anf is a name for both nostrils together, and each one is called a minkhar, not an anf. Among the paired is al-kaff (the palm), which is feminine. Al-Mubarrad claimed that it is sometimes masculine and recited:
ولو كفي اليمين تقيك خوفا ... لأفردت اليمين عن الشمال
(Even if my right hand were to protect you from fear, I would set the right apart from the left.)
— and he did not say al-yumnā; so al-Mubarrad said. But this is a mistake, because al-yamīn is feminine, like al-yumnā. Ibn Yasʿūn said: he made it masculine by construing it as "the member" (al-ʿuḍw), then returned to the feminine and said تقيك.
Whatever of the bodily members is unpaired is predominantly masculine; among the exceptions are al-lisān (the tongue) and al-qafā (the nape), which are sometimes feminine.

dervis-irab:62-64.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حَسْبَكَ): al-ḥasb, with sukūn on the sīn, is sufficiency. One says ḥasbuka dirham (a dirham suffices you), and the bāʾ may be added to it, so that one says bi-ḥasbika dirham, i.e. your sufficiency. One says: hādhā rajulun ḥasbuka min rajul (this is a man who is enough for you as a man), and Zayd ṣadīqī fa-ḥasbī or fa-ḥasb, i.e. he suffices me and makes others unnecessary. Jarīr said:
إني وجدت من المكارم حسبكم ... أن تلبسوا خز الثياب وتشبعوا
فإذا تذوكرت المكارم مرة ... في مجلس أنتم به فتقنعوا
(I have found that, of noble deeds, what suffices you is to wear silken garments and eat your fill; and when noble deeds are mentioned once in a gathering where you are, then veil your faces [in shame].)

* I'rab:
(وَإِنْ يُرِيدُوا أَنْ يَخْدَعُوكَ فَإِنَّ حَسْبَكَ اللَّهُ): the wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; يريدوا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); أن and what falls within its scope is a maṣdar (verbal noun) serving as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); فإن: the fāʾ links [the apodosis], and إنّ with its noun and its khabar (predicate) — the nominal clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).
(هُوَ الَّذِي أَيَّدَكَ بِنَصْرِهِ وَبِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ): هو is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and الذي its khabar; the clause أيدك is the ṣila (relative clause); بنصره is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أيدك; and بالمؤمنين is conjoined to بنصره.
(وَأَلَّفَ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِهِمْ): ألف is conjoined to أيدك; بين is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to ألف; and قلوبهم is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
(لَوْ أَنْفَقْتَ ما فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعاً ما أَلَّفْتَ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِهِمْ): لو is conditional; أنفقت is a verb and its agent; ما is the direct object; في الأرض is a naʿt (adjective); جميعا is a ḥāl (circumstantial); ما is negative; ألفت is a verb and its agent, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a condition that does not cause the jussive.
(وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ أَلَّفَ بَيْنَهُمْ إِنَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ): the wāw is a conjunction or resumptive; لكنّ and its noun, and the clause ألف بينهم is the khabar of لكن; إنّ with its noun and its two predicates, and the clause gives the reason (taʿlīliyya).
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ حَسْبُكَ اللَّهُ وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): حسبك is a khabar placed first and الله a mubtadaʾ placed after, or the reverse; من is conjoined to الله; the clause اتبعك is the ṣila; and من المؤمنين is a ḥāl.
The meaning is: Allah suffices you and the believers suffice you, i.e. Allah is sufficient for you and the believers are sufficient for you. [Translator's note: the source writes «وحسبك المؤمنين» with the accusative/genitive form, where the nominative المؤمنون would be expected; it then gives «وكافيك المؤمنون».] It may also be that [the wāw] has the sense of "with" (maʿa) and what follows it is accusative, as when you say ḥasbuka wa-Zaydan dirham; the meaning would then be: Allah is sufficient for you and sufficient for the believers. [This is] because conjoining an overt noun to a [genitive] attached pronoun in a case like this is not permitted, as is established in the science of grammar, though the Kufans allowed it. Al-Farrāʾ said: "It is not common in their speech to say ḥasbuka wa-akhīka; rather, what is used is ḥasbuka wa-ḥasbu akhīka, repeating the governing word. So if His words ومن اتبعك were genitive, it would have been said: ḥasbuka Allāhu wa-ḥasbu man ittabaʿaka." Al-Naḥḥās preferred the accusative as a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment).

* Benefits:
Ḥasb: Abū Ḥayyān said: Ḥasbuka is a mubtadaʾ annexed to the pronoun; it is neither a maṣdar nor an active participle.
Sībawayh said: "They said ḥasbuka wa-Zaydan dirham because it carries the meaning of kafāka (it sufficed you), and since it would be ugly to construe [Zayd] on the pronoun, they intended the verb, as though he had said: ḥasbuka wa-bi-ḥasbi akhāka dirham; and likewise kafyuka." Kafyuka is from kafāhu yakfīhi. Likewise qaṭṭuka: you say kafyuka wa-Zaydan dirham and qaṭṭuka wa-Zaydan dirham. [Translator's note: in the quotation the source reads «وبحسب أخاك», which appears garbled; Sībawayh's commonly cited wording is «حسبك ويحسب أخاك درهم», which fits the following explanation of yuḥsibu. Translated as written.] This is not of the category of the mafʿūl maʿahu; Sībawayh only brought it as evidence for construing on the verb because of what indicates it. Ḥasbuka indicates kafāka, and yuḥsibunī is the imperfect of aḥsabanī fulān, when he gives me until I say "enough for me" (ḥasbī). So what governs the accusative here is a verb indicated by the meaning; and in kafyuka wa-Zaydan dirham this is clearer, because [kafy] is the maṣdar of the implied verb, i.e. "and suffices Zayd". In qaṭṭuka wa-Zaydan dirham the implied construction is more remote, because nothing of the wording of qaṭṭuka is in the implied verb; it is explained only from the point of view of meaning. That implied verb has an agent referring to the dirham, and the dirham is intended to come first, so it becomes a case of conjoining clauses. It cannot be a case of iʿmāl (two governors competing for one word), because the mubtadaʾ's requiring the khabar and governing it is not of the kind of a verb's (or what functions like it) requiring and governing; so this should not be imagined here.
Al-Zajjāj said: "Ḥasb is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl), the kāf is accusative, and the wāw means 'with'." On this view, Allah is the agent of ḥasbuka, and on this construal ومن may be conjoined to the kāf, since it is an object of the verbal noun, not genitive, because a verbal noun is not annexed. However, al-Zajjāj's view is mistaken, because governing words enter upon ḥasbuka: you say bi-ḥasbika dirham, and the Exalted said: «فإن حسبك الله». Nor has it been established anywhere that it is a verbal noun, so that one might hold that it is sometimes a verbal noun and sometimes a noun that is not a verbal noun, like ruwayd.

dervis-irab:65-66.t:
* Vocabulary:
(حَرِّضِ): taḥrīḍ linguistically is urging something on with great insistence. It comes from al-ḥaraḍ, which is when illness wears someone down and grows severe in him until he is on the verge of death; or [taḥrīḍ is] that you call him ḥaraḍ and say to him: "I see you as nothing but ḥaraḍ (worn out, useless) in this matter", and muḥarriḍ in it, in order to stir him up and move him. One says ḥarrakahu, ḥarraḍahu, ḥarraṣahu, ḥarrashahu and ḥarrabahu with the same meaning. In al-Miṣbāḥ: ḥariḍa ḥaraḍan — of the pattern taʿiba — he was close to perishing, so he is ḥaraḍ, with fatḥa on the rāʾ, being named by the maṣdar (verbal noun) for intensity; and ḥarraḍtuhu ʿalā al-shayʾ taḥrīḍan (I urged him to the thing). In al-Mukhtār: taḥrīḍ to fighting is urging and heating [people] up for it.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ حَرِّضِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَى الْقِتالِ): حرض is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent) is "you" (anta); المؤمنين is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and على القتال is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) حرض.
(إِنْ يَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ عِشْرُونَ صابِرُونَ يَغْلِبُوا مِائَتَيْنِ): إن is conditional; يكن is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); منكم is the khabar (predicate) of يكن placed first, and عشرون its noun placed after; صابرون is a naʿt (adjective); يغلبوا is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and مئتين is the direct object. It is also possible to parse يكن here as complete (tāmma), so that عشرون is its agent and منكم a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(وَإِنْ يَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ مِائَةٌ يَغْلِبُوا أَلْفاً مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): conjoined to what preceded, and the i'rab is the same; من الذين كفروا is an adjective of «ألفا».
(بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لا يَفْقَهُونَ): بأنهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يغلبوا, the bāʾ being causal; أنّ and its noun, and قوم is its khabar; and the clause لا يفقهون is an adjective of «قوم».
(الْآنَ خَفَّفَ اللَّهُ عَنْكُمْ): الآن is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to خفف; الله is the agent; and عنكم is attached to خفف.
(وَعَلِمَ أَنَّ فِيكُمْ ضَعْفاً): conjoined to خفف; أنّ and what falls within its scope stand in place of the two objects of علم; فيكم is the khabar of أنّ placed first, and ضعفا its noun placed after.
(فَإِنْ يَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ مِائَةٌ صابِرَةٌ يَغْلِبُوا مِائَتَيْنِ): it has the i'rab given above.
(وَإِنْ يَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ أَلْفٌ يَغْلِبُوا أَلْفَيْنِ): conjoined to what preceded.
(بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ): بإذن الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يغلبوا; الله is the mubtadaʾ (subject); مع is an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar; and الصابرين is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

dervis-irab:67-69.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يُثْخِنَ): In al-Miṣbāḥ: "Athkhana fī al-arḍ ithkhānan: he marched against the enemy and slew them extensively; and athkhantuhu: I weakened him with wounds and enfeebled him." Athkhanahu al-maraḍ: the illness weighed him down. It is from al-thakhāna, which is thickness and density. The meaning is: until he humiliates disbelief and weakens it by spreading slaughter among its people, and strengthens Islam and makes it mighty by conquest and subjugation, with captivity coming after that.
(عَرَضَ الدُّنْيا): its paltry goods. It is so called because it lasts only a short while; He means the ransom. The theologians (al-mutakallimūn) called accidents aʿrāḍ because they have no permanence: they occur in bodies and then pass away from them.

* I'rab:
(ما كانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أَنْ يَكُونَ لَهُ أَسْرى): ما is negative; كان is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; لنبي is a khabar (predicate) placed first; and أن with what falls within its scope is its noun. It may also be complete (tāmma), meaning "it did not come about" and "it was not right", so that the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to it and أن with what falls within its scope is its fāʿil (agent). And يكون, its khabar placed first and its noun placed after. [Translator's note: the source's sentence here is elliptical — «ويكون وخبرها المقدم واسمها المؤخر»; the intended sense is evidently that in يكون له أسرى, له is the khabar of يكون placed first and أسرى its noun placed after.]
(حَتَّى يُثْخِنَ فِي الْأَرْضِ): حتى is a particle of limit and of the genitive; يثخن is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى; and في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يثخن.
(تُرِيدُونَ عَرَضَ الدُّنْيا): the clause is resumptive, and عرض الدنيا is the object of تريدون.
(وَاللَّهُ يُرِيدُ الْآخِرَةَ وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive or a conjunction; الله is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause يريد الآخرة is the khabar; الله is a mubtadaʾ, عزيز a first khabar and حكيم a second khabar.
(لَوْلا كِتابٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ سَبَقَ لَمَسَّكُمْ فِيما أَخَذْتُمْ عَذابٌ عَظِيمٌ): لولا is a particle of non-occurrence due to existence (imtināʿ li-wujūd), containing the sense of a condition; كتاب is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted; من الله is a naʿt (adjective) of كتاب, and likewise سبق; the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "exists" (mawjūd). لمسكم: the lām occurs in the apodosis of لولا, and مسكم is a verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); فيما is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to مسكم, i.e. "because of what you took"; ما is in a genitive construct [with the preposition], and أخذتم is the ṣila (relative clause); عذاب is the agent and عظيم an adjective.
(فَكُلُوا مِمَّا غَنِمْتُمْ حَلالًا طَيِّباً وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (fāʾ that reveals an implied condition), i.e. "since I have made the spoils lawful for you, eat"; كلوا is an imperative verb and its agent; مما is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to كلوا; the clause غنمتم is the ṣila; حلالا is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of what was taken as spoil, or as an adjective of the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a lawful eating"; اتقوا is conjoined to كلوا; the name of Majesty is the direct object; and إنّ with its noun and its two predicates.

* Rhetoric:
Ḥusn al-taʿlīl (elegant attribution of cause):
In the words of the Exalted «لولا كتاب من الله سبق لمسكم فيما أخذتم عذاب عظيم» there is a figure called "the figure of causation" (fann al-taʿlīl). It is that the speaker, wishing to mention a ruling that has occurred or is expected, first puts forward the cause of its occurrence before mentioning it, because the cause's rank is to precede what it causes. The prior decree from Allah the Exalted is the cause of the escape from punishment.
Further, with respect to the cause and the attribute that is given a cause, this figure is divided into four types:
1- [An attribute that is] established, with an evident cause, but [the poet gives a cause] different from the real cause. Its example is the words of Ibn al-Muʿtazz:
قالوا: اشتكت عينه، فقلت لهم: ... من كثرة القتل نالها الوصب
حمرتها من دماء من قتلت ... والدم في السيف شاهد عجب
(They said: His eye is ailing. I said to them: From so much killing has the ailment befallen it; its redness is from the blood of those it has slain — and blood on a sword is a wondrous witness.)
The real cause of the eye's redness is ophthalmia, which is evident; the poet left it aside and gave an unreal cause, namely that its redness is from the blood of the lovers it has slain.
2- Established, with a hidden cause, as in the words of Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī:
لم يحك نائلك السحاب وإنما ... حمّت به فصبيبها الرّحضاء
(The clouds did not imitate your bounty; rather, they caught a fever from it, and what pours from them is the sweat of fever.)
He means that the clouds did not imitate your bounty, i.e. your giving; rather they became feverish because of your bounty and its superiority over them, so that what pours from them is the sweat of fever. The descent of rain from the clouds is an established attribute whose cause does not usually appear, and he gave as its cause that it is the sweat of their fever brought on by the giving of the one praised.
3- [Not established but] possible, as in the words of Muslim ibn al-Walīd, known as Ṣarīʿ al-Ghawānī:
يا واشيا حسنت فينا إساءته ... نجى حذارك إنساني من الغرق
(O slanderer whose ill-doing toward us has proved good: wariness of you has saved the pupil of my eye from drowning.)
Finding the slanderer's ill-doing good is an attribute that is not established, yet it is possible. He went against people in finding it good, giving as the reason that his wariness of the slanderer was the cause of the pupil of his eye being saved from drowning in tears, since he gave up weeping out of fear of him. [Translator's note: the source heads this type «ثابت وهو متمكن» ("established and possible"), but its own explanation calls the attribute «غير ثابت إلا أنه ممكن» ("not established, yet possible"); the bracketed wording follows the explanation.]
4- The fourth type is neither established nor possible, as in the words of the poet:
لو لم تكن نية الجوزاء خدمته ... لما رأيت عليها عقد منتطق
(Had it not been the intention of Gemini to serve him, you would not see upon it the knotted belt of one girded [for service].)
Attributing intention to Gemini is neither established nor possible, for will comes only from a living being, and Gemini is an inanimate thing having no life, no will and no intention; yet the poet attributed this to it and gave as its cause the sign of service, namely the knotted belt — because the figure of Gemini is that of a person who has girded himself. Al-niṭāq is the girdle (zunnār) and anything with which the waist is bound.
It is clear that the noble verse does not fall within the scope of these four types, which are not free of artificiality; rather, it belongs to causation in general for one of the rulings.

dervis-irab:27-29.t:
* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَخُونُوا اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ): لا is prohibitive; تخونوا is an imperfect in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the Name of Majesty is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and الرسول is conjoined to الله. (وَتَخُونُوا أَماناتِكُمْ وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ): the wāw may be the wāw of accompaniment (wāw al-maʿiyya), so that «تخونوا» is in the accusative (manṣūb) by an أن implied after it, because it occurs as the response to the prohibition; or it may be conjunctive, so that «تخونوا» is in the jussive, falling under the ruling of the prohibition. Perhaps the second is preferable, because it contains a prohibition of each one separately, unlike the first, which contains a prohibition of combining the two; and prohibiting the combination of two things does not entail prohibiting each one separately. أماناتكم is a mafʿūl bihi on the assumption of an omitted word, i.e. "the owners of your trusts". The discussion of the metaphor of betrayal will come in the section on rhetoric. وأنتم: the wāw is for the ḥāl (circumstantial); أنتم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause تعلمون is the khabar (predicate); the clause أنتم تعلمون is circumstantial. The object of يعلمون is omitted because it is known, i.e. you know that what has come from you is betrayal.
(وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّما أَمْوالُكُمْ وَأَوْلادُكُمْ فِتْنَةٌ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ):
اعلموا is conjoined to what precedes; أنّما is [أنّ] made inoperative (kāffa wa-makfūfa), and it stands in place of the two objects of اعلموا, which is why its hamza takes fatḥa. The discussion of the hamza of إنّ with fatḥa and kasra will come in the section on benefits. أموالكم is a mubtadaʾ, أولادكم is conjoined to «أموالكم», and فتنة is the khabar. Wealth and children were made a fitna because they are a cause of falling into fitna, which is sin and punishment; or [fitna is] a trial and test from Allah, to sound your depths and fathom your reality. So — the matter being thus — there is nothing for you but to settle your souls on sincerity and on renouncing the ornaments of this world, and not to be deceived by its vanities and its passing sips. وأن الله is conjoined to أنما أموالكم وأولادكم: أنّ and its noun; عنده, the adverb, is a khabar placed first; أجر is a mubtadaʾ placed after; and the clause is the khabar of «أنّ». In this there is what turns you away from love of this world and preferring it to what is with Allah, which is better and more lasting. And in all this there is an urging to earn reward, a good report and an everlasting remembrance.
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ تَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ فُرْقاناً): إن is conditional; تتقوا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) يجعل; فرقانا is a mafʿūl bihi, i.e. a victory that distinguishes between truth and falsehood, and between disbelief, by humiliating its partisans, and Islam, by strengthening its supporters; or a deliverance from the doubts in which consciences swerve, understandings go astray, and eyes grow dim to seeing the truth.
Now, there is disagreement about «الفرقان» here. Some said: it is that by which truth and falsehood are distinguished, and the meaning is that He gives them such firmness of heart, penetration of insight and good guidance that they distinguish between the two when they are confused. It is also said:
الفرقان is the way out of doubts and deliverance from everything they fear. From this is the saying of the poet:
مالك من طول الأسى فرقان ... بعد قطين رحلوا وبانوا
(Gloss: You have no escape from long grief after the household who departed and went far away.)
And from it is the saying of another:
وكيف أرجّي الخلّ والموت طالبي ... ومالي من كأس المنية فرقان
(Gloss: How can I place hope in a friend when death is seeking me, and I have no escape from the cup of death?)
al-Farrāʾ said: what is meant by الفرقان is conquest and victory. Ibn Isḥāq said:
الفرقان is the separation between truth and falsehood. al-Suddī said: الفرقان is deliverance.
(وَيُكَفِّرْ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئاتِكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ): conjoined to what preceded. (وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ): the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ, ذو الفضل is its khabar, and العظيم is a naʿt (adjective) of الفضل.

* Rhetoric:
Istiʿāra (metaphor) in «لا تخونوا أماناتكم»: الخون originally means diminution; from it is تخوّنه, when he diminished it. Then it was borrowed for what is the opposite of trustworthiness and fidelity, because when you betray a man in something, you have brought diminution upon him.
It has also been borrowed in their saying: خان الدلو الكرب (the karab betrayed the bucket). الكرب, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ, is a rope tied at the top of the bucket. And: خان المشتار السبب (the rope betrayed the honey-gatherer); المشتار is the gatherer of honey, and السبب is the rope. When the rope breaks in both cases, it is as if it لم يقف [Translator's note: so in the source; probably a misprint for لم يفِ, "did not keep faith"]. The metaphor here is an explicit (taṣrīḥiyya) and derivative (tabaʿiyya) metaphor.

* Benefits:
The places where the hamza of إنّ takes kasra:
The hamza of (إنّ) must take kasra wherever a maṣdar (verbal noun) cannot properly stand in place of it and of what it governs. That is in twelve places:
1- When it occurs at the beginning of speech, actually, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «إنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر», or virtually, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «ألا إن أولياء الله لا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون».
2- When it occurs after «حيث», as in: اجلس حيث إن العلم موجود (sit where knowledge is present).
3- When it occurs after «إذ», as in: جئتك إذ إن الشمس تطلع (I came to you when the sun was rising).
4- When it follows a relative noun, as in «وآتيناه من الكنوز ما إن مفاتحه لتنوء بالعصبة أولي القوة».
5- When it occurs as the response to an oath, as in: والله إن العلم نور (by Allah, knowledge is light), and the saying of Allah the Exalted: «والعصر إن الإنسان لفي خسر».
6- When it occurs after a verb of saying, quoted by it, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «قال: إني عبد الله». If the saying means thinking, it does not take kasra, as in: أتقول أن عبد الله يقول كذا? (do you say that ʿAbd Allāh says such-and-such?), i.e. do you think. And if it is not quoted by the saying, it also does not take kasra, as in: أخصك بالقول أنك فاضل (I single you out with speech, because you are excellent); here it has the sense of giving a reason, i.e. لأنك فاضل (because you are excellent), so it, together with what falls in its scope, is in the accusative by removal of the preposition.
7- When it occurs, together with what follows it, as a ḥāl, as in: جئت وإن الشمس تغرب (I came while the sun was setting); from it is the saying of Allah the Exalted: «كما أخرجك ربك من بيتك بالحق، وإن فريقا من المؤمنين لكارهون».
8- When it occurs, together with what follows it, as a naʿt of what precedes it, as in: جاء رجل إنه فاضل (a man came who is excellent).
9- When it occurs at the head of a resumptive clause, as in: فلان يزعم أني أسأت إليه، إنه لكاذب (so-and-so claims that I wronged him; he is surely a liar). This is among the cases of occurring at the beginning.
10- When the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ), or the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) as the grammarians call it, occurs in its khabar, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «والله يعلم إنك لرسوله، والله يشهد إن المنافقين لكاذبون».
11- When it occurs, together with what falls in its scope, as the khabar of a noun denoting a concrete entity, as in: علي إنه فهفل [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently a misprint for فاضل — "ʿAlī, he is excellent"]. From it is the saying of Allah the Exalted: «إن الذين آمنوا والذين هادوا والصابئين والنصارى والمجوس والذين أشركوا إن الله يفصل بينهم»; the clause:
«إن الله يفصل بينهم» is the khabar of إنّ الذين آمنوا and what is conjoined to it, because they are [concrete] nouns.
12- When it occurs after the deterrent «كلّا», as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «كلا إن الإنسان ليطغى».

The places where the hamza of أنّ takes fatḥa:
The hamza of (أنّ) must take fatḥa wherever a maṣdar can properly stand in place of it and of its two governed elements. That is in eleven places:
1- When it, together with what falls in its scope, is in the position of the fāʿil, as in: بلغني أنك مجتهد (it reached me that you are diligent); from it is the saying of Allah the Exalted: «أولم يكفهم أنا أنزلنا عليك الكتاب».
Of this kind is its occurring after «لو», as in «ولو أنهم آمنوا واتقوا لمثوبة من عند الله خير»: what follows «أنّ» is interpreted as a maṣdar in the nominative, the fāʿil of an omitted verb whose implied form is ثبت (it were established); the lām is the lām of the response, so the clause after it is the apodosis of «لو».
2- When it, together with what falls in its scope, is in the position of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «قل أوحي إلي أنه استمع نفر من الجن», i.e. the listening of a group.
3- When it, together with what falls in its scope, is in the position of the mubtadaʾ, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «ومن آياته أنك ترى الأرض خاشعة»: the preposition and its genitive noun are a khabar placed first, and what follows «أنّ» is interpreted as a maṣdar, a mubtadaʾ placed after, i.e. your seeing the earth humbled is among His signs.
4- When it, together with what follows it, is in the position of the khabar of an abstract noun (ism maʿnā) that is not [a word of] saying and of which its khabar is not true, i.e. [its khabar is not true] of the abstract noun, as in: اعتقادي أنه فاضل (my belief is that he is excellent). It must take fatḥa because it is the khabar of «اعتقادي», which is an abstract noun, not [a word of] saying, and its khabar is not true of اعتقادي, because «فاضل» is not true of belief.
It takes fatḥa only because the maṣdar stands in place of it and its two governed elements; the implied form is: اعتقادي فضله (my belief is his excellence), i.e. what I believe is that. Its kasra is not allowed, so that it would, with its two governed elements, be a clause predicated of اعتقادي, because there is no binding element (rābiṭ): the noun of «أنّ» does not refer back to the mubtadaʾ, which is اعتقادي, since its khabar is not true of it; it refers to something else, so the clause remains without a binding element. This is unlike: قولي: إنه فاضل (my saying is: he is excellent), where it must take kasra, because it occurs as the khabar of «قولي» and needs no binding element, since when the clause is intended as a quotation of its wording, it is the mubtadaʾ itself in meaning; the implied sense is: my saying is this wording and no other. And it is unlike: «اعتقاد زيد إنه حق» (Zayd's belief — it is true), where the hamza of «إنه» must also take kasra, because its khabar is true of the belief, and nothing prevents the clause of إنّ and its two governed elements from occurring as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, since the noun of إنّ binds them. It is not correct to give it fatḥa, because it would become: "Zayd's belief is his belief's being true", and that conveys nothing, because the khabar must convey what is not conveyed by the mubtadaʾ.
5- When it, together with what falls in its scope, is in the position of something following a nominative, as conjoined to it or as a badal (substitute) for it, as in: بلغني اجتهادك وأنك حسن الخلق (your diligence and that you are of good character reached me), interpreted as: your diligence and your good character reached me, so it is conjoined to it; and as in: يعجبني سعيد أنه مجتهد (Saʿīd pleases me — that he is diligent), interpreted as: Saʿīd pleases me, his diligence; so the interpreted maṣdar is a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from «سعيد».
6- When it, together with what falls in its scope, is in the position of the mafʿūl bihi, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «ولا تخافون أنكم أشركتم بالله», interpreted as: and you do not fear your associating partners.
7- When it, together with what falls in its scope, is in the position of the khabar of kāna or one of its sisters, as in: كان يقيني أنك تتبع الحق (my certainty was that you follow the truth), interpreted as: my certainty was your following the truth.
8- When it, together with what falls in its scope, is in the position of something following an accusative, by conjunction or as a badal, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «اذكروا نعمتي التي أنعمت عليكم وأني فضلتكم على العالمين», the implied form being: remember My favour upon you and My preferring you.
And the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وإذ يعدكم الله إحدى الطائفتين أنها لكم», the implied form being, as mentioned before: He promises you one of the two parties, its being yours; so what follows أنّ is interpreted as a maṣdar in the accusative, a badal of inclusion from إحدى.
9- When it occurs after a preposition, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «ذلك بأن الله هو الحق».
10- When it, together with what falls in its scope, occurs in the position of the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «إنه لحق مثلما أنكم تنطقون», i.e. like your speaking.
11- When it, together with what falls in its scope, occurs in the position of something following a genitive, by conjunction or as a badal, as in: سررت من أدب علي وأنه عاقل (I was pleased with ʿAlī's manners and that he is intelligent), the implied form being: I was pleased with ʿAlī's manners and his intelligence; and as in: عجبت منه أنه مهمل (I wondered at him, that he is negligent), the implied form being: عجيب منه إهماله, and the meaning: I wondered at his negligence. So what follows «أنّ» is interpreted as a maṣdar in the genitive, a badal of inclusion from the hāʾ in «منه».
The places where both kasra and fatḥa are allowed:
Both are allowed — kasra and fatḥa of the hamza of إنّ — wherever both considerations are valid:
interpretation as a maṣdar and non-interpretation. That is in nine places:
1- After the «إذا» of surprise (al-fujāʾiyya), as in: خرجت فإذا أن سعيدا واقف (I went out, and lo, Saʿīd was standing). Kasra is in the sense: فإذا سعيد واقف (and lo, Saʿīd is standing); fatḥa is on interpreting what follows it as a maṣdar, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, the interpretation being: فإذا وقوفه حاصل (and lo, his standing is present).
The saying of the poet has been transmitted both ways:
وكنت أرى زيدا، كما قيل سيدا ... إذا أنه عبد القفا واللهازم
(Gloss: I used to think Zayd, as was said, a master — and lo, he is a slave of the nape and the jaw-bones.)
Sībawayh cited it without attributing it to anyone. أرى is with ḍamma on the hamza; its origin is: يريني الله (Allah shows me). The well-known procedure was applied to it — giving ḍamma to its first letter, fatḥa to the letter before the last, and omitting the agent — and in addition, here the yāʾ was replaced with a hamza out of necessity, because when the agent was omitted and the object made deputy, the verb had to be predicated of the pronoun of the speaker, and only a verb beginning with hamza can be predicated of it; so the yāʾ was dropped and the hamza brought in its place. It takes three objects: the first is the deputy agent, the second is «زيدا», and the third is «سيدا»; the clause «كما قيل» is parenthetical. Kasra is in the sense of a clause, i.e. and lo, he is a slave of the nape; fatḥa is in the sense of a single word, i.e. and lo, servitude is present, making it a mubtadaʾ whose khabar has been omitted, as you say: خرجت فإذا الأسد (I went out, and lo, the lion), i.e. is present. اللهازم is the plural of لهزمة, with kasra on the lām and the zāy; it is a bone protruding below the ear. The meaning is: I used to suppose him a master, but when I looked at his nape and jaw-bones, his servitude became clear to me; he alluded to that by [saying] that he is struck on his nape and his jaw-bones, the nape being the place of slapping.
2- After the fāʾ of the requital (fāʾ al-jazāʾ), as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «من عمل منكم سوءا بجهالة ثم تاب من بعده وأصلح فإنه غفور رحيم», which was read with kasra and with fatḥa of «إنّ». Kasra is on making what follows the fāʾ of the requital [Translator's note: the source has «فاء الجزء», evidently a misprint for «فاء الجزاء»] a complete clause, the meaning being: forgiveness and mercy are present; fatḥa is on taking أنّ and its two governed elements as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, the meaning being: what is present is forgiveness and mercy; or as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, the meaning being: forgiveness and mercy are present.
3- When it occurs, together with what falls in its scope, in the position of giving a reason, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted:
«صل عليهم إن صلاتك سكن لهم»: kasra is on its being a causal clause, and fatḥa on implying the causal lām that governs the genitive, i.e. because your prayer is a reassurance for them.
From it is the noble hadith: «لبيك إن الحمد والنعمة لك» (Here I am at Your service; [indeed / because] praise and favour are Yours), which is transmitted with kasra and with fatḥa of «إنّ»: kasra on its being a resumptive giving of reason, and fatḥa on implying the lām of cause.
4- When it occurs after a verb of oath with no lām after it, as in the saying of Ruʾba:
أو تحلفي بربك العليّ ... أني أبو ذيّالك الصّبي
(Gloss: Or you swear by your Lord the Most High that I am the father of that little boy.)
It is transmitted with kasra and with fatḥa of «إنّ»: kasra as the response to the oath, and fatḥa by implying «على».
5- When it occurs as the khabar of [a word of] saying, and is itself predicated with a saying, the speaker of both sayings being one, as in: قولي أني أحمد الله (my saying is that I praise Allah), with fatḥa and with kasra on the hamza of «أنّ». Fatḥa is on its proper maṣdar sense, i.e. my saying is praise of Allah; kasra is in the sense of what is said, i.e. what I say is: I praise Allah.
6- When it occurs after a wāw preceded by a single word fit to be conjoined to, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «إن لك أن لا تجوع فيها ولا تعرى وأنك لا تظمأ ولا تضحى». Nāfiʿ and Abū Bakr read it with kasra in «وإنك لا تظمأ», either as resumption or as conjunction to the first «إنّ» clause; on both views it has no grammatical position.
The rest of the Seven read it with fatḥa, conjoined to «أن لا يجوع» [Translator's note: so in the source; the ayah has تجوع], as a single word conjoined to its like, the implied form being: that for you there is no hunger and no thirst.
7- When it occurs after «حتى»: kasra is specific to the inceptive [حتى], as in:
مرض زيد حتى إنهم لا يرجونه (Zayd fell ill, so much so that they have no hope for him); and fatḥa is specific to the [حتى] that governs the genitive and the conjunctive one, as in: عرفت أمورك حتى أنك فاضل (I came to know your affairs, even that you are excellent). «حتى» in this example can be a preposition or a conjunction, and أنّ in both takes fatḥa.
8- When it occurs after «أما» with fatḥa on the hamza and a single mīm, as in:
أما أنك فاضل (truly, you are excellent). Kasra is on «أما» being an opening particle (ḥarf istiftāḥ), like «ألا», after which «إنّ» takes kasra; fatḥa is on its being compounded of the interrogative hamza and the general «ما» meaning "a thing", the two together, after compounding, meaning: أحقا (is it true that…).
9- When it occurs after «لا جرم», as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «لا جرم أن الله يعلم ما يسرون». Fatḥa is predominant; its explanation is that what follows «أنّ» is interpreted as a maṣdar in the nominative, the fāʿil of جرم, and جرم means "it is established and true". The root meaning of الجرم is cutting; and Allah's knowledge of things is decisively certain (maqṭūʿ bihi), because it is true and established. لا is a particle of negation used as an answer, by which preceding speech is meant; so it is as if He said: "No", i.e. the matter is not as they claimed; then He said: جرم أن الله يعلم, i.e. His knowledge is true and established.
More will be said about «لا جرم» when it is discussed in its place.
A necessary caution:
Wherever both fatḥa and kasra of «إنّ» are allowed, kasra is preferable and more frequent, because it involves no artificiality, except when it occurs after «لا جرم», as you have learned.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ قُلْ لِمَنْ فِي أَيْدِيكُمْ مِنَ الْأَسْرى): لمن is [a preposition and its genitive noun] attached to (mutaʿalliq) قل; في أيديكم is the ṣila (relative clause) of من; and من الأسرى is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(إِنْ يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ خَيْراً): إن is conditional; يعلم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); الله is the fāʿil (agent); في قلوبكم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of يعلم and خيرا a second object; and the conditional clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the verb "say").
(يُؤْتِكُمْ خَيْراً مِمَّا أُخِذَ مِنْكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): يؤتكم is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the kāf is the first object and خيرا the second object; مما is attached to «خيرا»; the clause أخذ is the ṣila; منكم is attached to أخذ; يغفر لكم is conjoined to يؤتكم; الله is the mubtadaʾ (subject), غفور a first khabar (predicate) and رحيم a second khabar.
