(وَإِنْ يُرِيدُوا خِيانَتَكَ فَقَدْ خانُوا اللَّهَ مِنْ قَبْلُ): the wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; يريدوا is the protasis and the wāw is the agent; خيانتك is the direct object; the fāʾ links the apodosis; قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); خانوا الله is a verb, its agent and its object; من قبل is attached to خانوا. قبل is indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is cut off from annexation in wording but not in meaning, i.e. before Badr, through disbelief.
(فَأَمْكَنَ مِنْهُمْ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; أمكن is a past verb with a latent (mustatir) agent; منهم is attached to أمكن; the object of أمكن is omitted, i.e. "He gave you power over them"; and الله is a mubtadaʾ with its two predicates.
(إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَهاجَرُوا وَجاهَدُوا بِأَمْوالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): إنّ and its noun; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila, and the verbs after it are conjoined to it.
(وَالَّذِينَ آوَوْا وَنَصَرُوا أُولئِكَ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِياءُ بَعْضٍ): والذين is conjoined to الذين; the clause آووا is the ṣila and نصروا is conjoined to آووا; أولئك is a mubtadaʾ, بعضهم a second mubtadaʾ and أولياء بعض its khabar; the second mubtadaʾ with its khabar is the khabar of the first mubtadaʾ; and the clause أولئك ... etc. is the khabar of إنّ.
(وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَلَمْ يُهاجِرُوا ما لَكُمْ مِنْ وَلايَتِهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ حَتَّى يُهاجِرُوا): والذين conjoins a clause to a clause. الذين is a mubtadaʾ; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila; لم يهاجروا is conjoined to آمنوا, or the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ما is negative; لكم is a khabar placed first; من ولايتهم is a ḥāl, because it was originally an adjective of شيء; من is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition and شيء is a mubtadaʾ placed after, by position; the clause ما لكم is the khabar of الذين. حتى is a particle of limit and of the genitive; يهاجروا is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى; and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to the verbal sense contained in the negation, i.e. "your guardianship over them is negated until their emigration". [Translator's note: the source reads «ابتغت ولايتك», apparently a misprint for «انتفت ولايتكم» ("your guardianship is negated"); translated according to the evident sense.]
(وَإِنِ اسْتَنْصَرُوكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ فَعَلَيْكُمُ النَّصْرُ): the wāw is a conjunction; إن is conditional; استنصروكم is a verb, its agent and its object, in the position of the jussive (majzūm) as the protasis; في الدين is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to استنصروكم; the fāʾ links [the apodosis]; عليكم is a khabar placed first and النصر a mubtadaʾ placed after; and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis.
(إِلَّا عَلى قَوْمٍ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ مِيثاقٌ وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ): إلا is a particle of exception; على قوم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted excepted [term], i.e. "except help against a people"; بينكم is an adverb (ẓarf) attached to an omitted khabar placed first; بينهم is conjoined to بينكم; ميثاق is a mubtadaʾ placed after; and the nominal clause is a naʿt (adjective) of قوم — i.e. as for these people, do not help them [the believers who did not emigrate] against them and so break the covenant. الله is a mubtadaʾ and بصير its khabar, and بما تعملون is attached to بصير.

dervis-irab:73-75.t:
* I'rab:
(وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِياءُ بَعْضٍ): the wāw is a conjunction; الذين is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and كفروا the ṣila (relative clause); بعضهم is a second mubtadaʾ and أولياء is the khabar (predicate) of بعضهم, and the clause is the khabar of الذين. It is also possible that بعضهم is a badal (substitute) of the demonstrative, with أولياء بعض as the khabar. [Translator's note: there is no demonstrative in this phrase; the remark seems carried over from verse 72 (أولئك بعضهم أولياء بعض), and here would apply to الذين. Translated as written.]
(إِلَّا تَفْعَلُوهُ تَكُنْ فِتْنَةٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَفَسادٌ كَبِيرٌ): إن is conditional and لا is redundant (zāʾida); تفعلوه is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); تكن is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and it is complete (tāmma); فتنة is the agent, i.e. "strife will come about"; في الأرض is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) تكن; فساد is conjoined to فتنة; and كبير is a naʿt (adjective) of فتنة. [Translator's note: إلا here is إن + لا, so لا is the negative particle (if you do not do it), not redundant; and كبير, being masculine, qualifies فساد rather than فتنة. Translated as written.]
(وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَهاجَرُوا وَجاهَدُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ): الذين is a mubtadaʾ, آمنوا is the ṣila, and what follows it is conjoined to it.
(وَالَّذِينَ آوَوْا وَنَصَرُوا): conjoined to الذين آمنوا.
(أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ حَقًّا): أولئك is a mubtadaʾ; هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a second mubtadaʾ; المؤمنون is the khabar of أولئك, or the khabar of «هم» with the clause being the khabar of أولئك; and حقا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
(لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَرِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ): لهم is a khabar placed first and مغفرة a mubtadaʾ placed after; رزق is conjoined to مغفرة and كريم is an adjective.
(وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْ بَعْدُ وَهاجَرُوا وَجاهَدُوا مَعَكُمْ): الذين is a mubtadaʾ, آمنوا is the ṣila, and what follows it is conjoined to it.
(فَأُولئِكَ مِنْكُمْ): the fāʾ links [the predicate], because of the hint of condition in the relative noun; the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and منكم its khabar.
(وَأُولُوا الْأَرْحامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلى بِبَعْضٍ فِي كِتابِ اللَّهِ): أولو is a nominative (marfūʿ) mubtadaʾ, the sign of its nominative being the wāw because it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural; الأرحام is the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); بعضهم is a mubtadaʾ and أولى its khabar; ببعض is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أولى; and في كتاب الله is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "this ruling is mentioned in the Book of Allah".
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ): إنّ and its noun; بكل شيء is attached to عليم; and عليم is the khabar of إنّ.

dervis-irab:30-31.t:
* Vocabulary:
(أَساطِيرُ): the plural of أسطورة, like أحدوثة and أحاديث: what has been lined up (suṭira) and written of stories and reports.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ يَمْكُرُ بِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِيُثْبِتُوكَ أَوْ يَقْتُلُوكَ أَوْ يُخْرِجُوكَ): the adverb is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an implied اذكر (remember); the meaning is: and remember, O Muḥammad, when those who disbelieved plotted against you. المكر is scheming to bring harm to others; the story of this plot is in the lengthy works. The clause يمكر is that to which the adverb is annexed; بك is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يمكر; الذين is the fāʿil (agent) of يمكر; the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; the lām is causal; يثبتوك is in the accusative (manṣūb) by an أن implied after the causal lām; أو يقتلوك is conjoined to it, and أو يخرجوك is also conjoined. The meaning is: remember when they gathered in Dār al-Nadwa — the first house built in Mecca — to restrain you, i.e. bind and imprison you, or to kill you, all of them, as the killing of one man, or to drive you out of Mecca. (وَيَمْكُرُونَ وَيَمْكُرُ اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الْماكِرِينَ):
the wāw is resumptive; يمكرون is an imperfect verb and the wāw is its fāʿil; ويمكر الله is conjoined; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and خير الماكرين its khabar (predicate). The discussion of this will come in the section on rhetoric. (وَإِذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ آياتُنا قالُوا قَدْ سَمِعْنا): the wāw is resumptive; إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of a condition; the clause تتلى is that to which the adverb is annexed; عليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تتلى; آياتنا is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause قالوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; the clause قد سمعنا is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). (لَوْ نَشاءُ لَقُلْنا مِثْلَ هذا): لو is conditional; نشاء is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the lām is linking; the clause قلنا has no [grammatical] position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition; مثل is a naʿt (adjective) of a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. a saying like this. (إِنْ هذا إِلَّا أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ): إن is negating; هذا is a mubtadaʾ; إلا is a particle of restriction; أساطير الأولين is the khabar of هذا.

* Rhetoric:
1- His saying «ويمكر الله» may be an istiʿāra tabaʿiyya (derivative metaphor), applying "plotting" to repelling: since the meaning of plotting is a stratagem by which harm is brought upon others, which is not permissible in the case of Allah the Exalted, what is meant by Allah's plotting is the repelling of their plot, i.e. making its outcome and its ill consequences fall upon them. It may also be of the type of mushākala (verbal correspondence) — its parallel has come before, as has the discussion of this device — i.e.:
what is meant by Allah's plotting is requiting them for their plot with something of its kind, by way of majāz mursal (metonymic trope), the relationship being causality. The speech may also be an istiʿāra tamthīliyya (extended metaphor), likening the state of تعليل المسلمين in their eyes [Translator's note: so in the source; probably a misprint for تقليل, i.e. making the Muslims appear few in their eyes], which led them on to their destruction, to the dealing of a scheming plotter who shows the opposite of what he conceals.
2- In the saying of Allah the Exalted «قد سمعنا لو نشاء لقلنا مثل هذا» there is a device called taghāyur (change of stance), which is the variance of two positions, either regarding a single meaning, such that a person praises something or blames it, or blames what another praised, or the reverse; or prefers one thing to another, then goes back and makes the inferior superior and the superior inferior. Reference to it has been made before, with examples of it. We say that the taghāyur meant here is their varying from themselves: Quraysh said about the Qur'an: «ما سمعنا بهذا في آبائنا الأولين» (we have not heard of this among our forefathers), rejecting it because of the strangeness of its style and the eloquence that dazzled them; and this statement entails their admission of inability to imitate it. Then Quraysh varied from itself and said: we have heard, «لو نشاء لقلنا مثل هذا». Had the two statements been at one time, that would have been a contradiction, which is a fault and would not be counted among the beauties [of style]; but its occurring at two different times and separate moments is counted among the beauties, and that is why it is called taghāyur and not contradiction.

dervis-irab:32-34.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ قالُوا اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كانَ هذا هُوَ الْحَقَّ مِنْ عِنْدِكَ): إذ is in the accusative by an omitted اذكر, and the discussion of it has been given fully before; the clause قالوا is that to which the adverb is annexed; اللهم is a vocative, a single proper name, from which «يا» has been omitted and compensated by the doubled mīm. إن is conditional; كان is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); هذا is its noun; هو is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); الحق is the khabar of كان; من عندك is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). (فَأَمْطِرْ عَلَيْنا حِجارَةً مِنَ السَّماءِ): the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa); أمطر is an imperative verb; علينا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أمطر; حجارة is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); من السماء is a naʿt (adjective) of حجارة; and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (أَوِ ائْتِنا بِعَذابٍ أَلِيمٍ): أو is a conjunction; ائت is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter, its agent latent (mustatir); بعذاب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ائتنا; أليم is a naʿt. (وَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ وَأَنْتَ فِيهِمْ): the wāw is resumptive; ما is negating; كان and its noun; the lām is the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd); يعذبهم is in the accusative by an أن implied after the lām of denial; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of كان. وأنت فيهم: the wāw is for the ḥāl, and the nominal clause of mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar is circumstantial. (وَما كانَ اللَّهُ مُعَذِّبَهُمْ وَهُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ): conjoined to the preceding clause; هم يستغفرون is in the position of a ḥāl. Its meaning is a negation of seeking forgiveness on their part, i.e. had they been among those who believe and seek forgiveness for disbelief, He would not have punished them; but they do not believe and do not seek forgiveness, and that is not expected of them.
(وَما لَهُمْ أَلَّا يُعَذِّبَهُمُ اللَّهُ): the wāw is conjunctive; ما is an interrogative noun of disapproval with the force of negation, a mubtadaʾ; لهم is the khabar; أن لا يعذبهم الله: أن together with what falls in its scope is a maṣdar in the accusative by removal of the preposition, attached to what the preceding preposition and its genitive noun are attached to, or to an omitted ḥāl, along the lines of the saying [of the poet]: تقول سليمى ما لجسمك شاحبا ... كأنك يحميك الطعام طبيب
(Gloss: Sulaymā says: What is with your body, pale, as though a doctor were keeping food from you?)
The meaning is: how should they not be punished, and what is established and settled for them so that they should not be punished? i.e. there is nothing to prevent His punishment from befalling them. (وَهُمْ يَصُدُّونَ عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرامِ): the wāw is for the ḥāl, and the clause هم يصدون is circumstantial; the meaning is: how should they not be punished, when their state is that they bar [people] from the Sacred Mosque, as they barred the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the year of al-Ḥudaybiya. (وَما كانُوا أَوْلِياءَهُ): the wāw is conjunctive or circumstantial; كانوا أولياءه: كان, its noun and its khabar. (إِنْ أَوْلِياؤُهُ إِلَّا الْمُتَّقُونَ): إن is negating; أولياؤه is a mubtadaʾ; إلا is a particle of restriction; المتقون is the khabar of «أولياؤه». (وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): لكنّ and its noun, and the clause is its khabar; the wāw is circumstantial or resumptive.

* Rhetoric:
In the saying of Allah the Exalted «وما كان الله ليعذبهم وأنت فيهم» etc. there is a remarkable device called «the device of tankīt (pointed choice)». Its definition is that the speaker deliberately mentions one thing rather than another that could take its place, because of a subtle point (nukta) in what is mentioned that makes its use preferable to anything else. For someone might say: what is the subtle point that made it preferable for the two forms to differ — the verb, «يعذبهم», and the active participle, «معذبهم» — rather than to agree, given that their times agree? For the period of the Messenger's ﷺ stay among those addressed is divided between the present and the future, and likewise the period of seeking forgiveness. Is it permissible for each of the two forms to come in the place (majāz) of the other, or is only what the messengers brought permissible? Or is it permissible to confine oneself to the verb, which indicates both times, without the active participle, or not? The answer — knowledge of the subtle point that made it preferable for the speech to come as it did, such that nothing else is permissible — is that those addressed by it are the hypocrites, for whom the Prophet ﷺ was not given leave to grant respite for the period of his stay among them, neither before the revelation of the ayah nor after it. A truthful report must correspond to what is reported. Since الرابع الذي أمر الخبير به [Translator's note: so in the source; this phrase appears to be corrupt, probably for «الواقع الذي أخبر الخبير به», "the reality which the All-Aware reported"] was the negation of their punishment in the past and the present and not the future — for the truthful report has informed about them in the future, where He said: «وما لهم أن لا يعذبهم الله» — eloquence required the use of the imperfect verb, which indicates, when unrestricted, both times, with a contextual indicator (qarīna) pointing to one of them according to what it indicates; and His saying «وأنت فيهم» was joined to it, so that it conveyed its indication of the present and not the future. And [since there was to be] a negation of [their] obtaining knowledge [Translator's note: so in the source; the sense appears to be "a negation of their punishment"] in the time that passed before the revelation of the ayah, He, glory be to Him, brought the form of the annexed active participle to indicate the past. Good ordering then required that He put the verb form first, because of its indication of the present, which is the period of his stay among them, since negating the punishment in that [period] is the more important. Instances of tankīt will come in the Qur'an that dazzle the mind.

dervis-irab:35-37.t:
* Vocabulary:
(المكاء): with ḍamma on the mīm, like الثغاء (bleating) and الرغاء (grumbling of camels); from مكا يمكو, when he whistled. From it is المكّاء (a bird, the lark), as if it were so named because of its much whistling. ʿAntara said:
وحليل غانية تركت مجدّلا ... تمكو فريصته كشدق الأعلم
(Gloss: Many a husband of a beautiful woman have I left thrown to the ground, his shoulder-muscle whistling like the cleft lip of the hare-lipped.)
i.e. many a husband of a woman of outstanding beauty, who needed no adornment because of her beauty, have I killed and thrown on the ground, and his shoulder-muscle was whistling with the gushing of blood from it, like the corner of the mouth of one with a cleft lip.
(التصدية): clapping. There is disagreement about its origin. It is said: it is from الصدى, which is the echo of sound heard in hard, empty places; from it one says: صدّى يصدّي تصدية; and what is meant by it here is the sound heard from clapping one hand on the other. It is also said: it is taken from التصدد, which is clamour, shouting and clapping, and one of the two dāls was changed into a yāʾ for lightness.
It is also said: it is from الصدّ, i.e. preventing, the original being تصددة, also with two dāls, and the second of them was changed into a yāʾ.
Ibn Yaʿīsh said: «As for التصدية in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وما كان صلاتهم عند البيت إلا مكاء وتصدية», the yāʾ is a substitute for the dāl, because it is from صدّ يصدّ, which is clapping and making noise; from it is the saying of Allah the Exalted: «إذا قومك منه يصدّون», i.e. they clamour and shout. So one of the two dāls was turned into a yāʾ. This is the view of Abū ʿUbayda. al-Rustamī rejected this view and said: it is only from الصدى, which is sound. The first view is not impossible, since يصدّون applies to sound or a kind of it; and if that is so, it is not impossible that تصدية be from it, so that it is of the pattern «تفعلة», like التحة [Translator's note: so in the source; probably a misprint for التحلّة] and التعلّة. When the second dāl was changed into a yāʾ, assimilation became impossible because the two sounds differ.»
(ركمه): He gathers it, piled one part upon another. In al-Mukhtār:
«ركم الشيء, when he gathered it and threw some of it upon some, of the pattern of نصر. ارتكم الشيء and تراكم: it gathered together. الركام, with ḍamma, is heaped-up sand, clouds and the like.»

* I'rab:
(وَما كانَ صَلاتُهُمْ عِنْدَ الْبَيْتِ إِلَّا مُكاءً وَتَصْدِيَةً): the wāw is resumptive or conjunctive; ما is negating; كان and its noun; عند البيت: the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); إلا is a particle of restriction; مكاء is the khabar (predicate) of كان, and تصدية is conjoined to مكاء. The meaning is that they put whistling and clapping in the place of prayer: they used to circumambulate the House naked, men and women, interlacing their fingers, whistling through them and clapping. This is an eloquent style among the styles of the Arabs, along the lines of the saying of al-Farazdaq:
وما كنت أرجو أن يكون عطاؤه ... أداهم سودا أو محدرجة حمرا
(Gloss: I did not expect that his gift would be black fetters or red twisted whips.)
i.e. I did not think that his gift would be black shackles or red twisted whips — it is also transmitted as «سمرا» (brown) — so he put shackles and whips in the place of a gift; and the poet put hoping in the place of thinking, and applied "gift" to punishment figuratively.
(فَذُوقُوا الْعَذابَ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (revealing an omitted condition); ذوقوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); العذاب is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the bāʾ is causal; ما is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), i.e.:
because of your disbelief. Parallels to it have come before. (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوالَهُمْ لِيَصُدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ):
إنّ and its noun; the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause); the clause ينفقون أموالهم is the khabar of الذين; ليصدوا: the lām is causal, and يصدوا is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن, the wāw being the fāʿil; عن سبيل الله is attached to يصدوا. (فَسَيُنْفِقُونَها ثُمَّ تَكُونُ عَلَيْهِمْ حَسْرَةً ثُمَّ يُغْلَبُونَ): the fāʾ is conjunctive; the sīn is a particle of futurity; ينفقونها is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; ثم is a conjunction of delay and sequence; تكون is conjoined to ينفقونها, and its noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being هي (it); عليهم is attached to an omitted ḥāl, because it was originally a naʿt (adjective) of حسرة and was placed first; حسرة is the khabar of تكون; ثم يغلبون is conjoined to ثم تكون, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِلى جَهَنَّمَ يُحْشَرُونَ): الذين is a mubtadaʾ (subject); كفروا is the ṣila; the clause يحشرون is the khabar of الذين; إلى جهنم is attached to يحشرون. (لِيَمِيزَ اللَّهُ الْخَبِيثَ مِنَ الطَّيِّبِ): the lām is causal, and يميز is in the accusative by an implied أن; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to one of the preceding verbs; الله is the fāʿil; الخبيث is a mafʿūl bihi; من الطيب is attached to يميز, i.e. the wicked party from the good party. (وَيَجْعَلَ الْخَبِيثَ بَعْضَهُ عَلى بَعْضٍ): يجعل is conjoined to يميز; الخبيث is its object; بعضه is a badal (substitute) for الخبيث, a badal of part for whole; على بعض is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, or in the position of an accusative as the second object of يجعل, the implied form being:
and He makes some of the wicked high upon others. (فَيَرْكُمَهُ جَمِيعاً فَيَجْعَلَهُ فِي جَهَنَّمَ): the fāʾ is conjunctive; يركمه is conjoined to يجعل, and the hāʾ is its object; جميعا is a ḥāl from the hāʾ in يركمه, or a tawkīd (emphasis) of it; فيجعله is conjoined to يركمه, and في جهنم is a second object. (أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْخاسِرُونَ): a mubtadaʾ and a khabar, هم being a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); or a first and a second mubtadaʾ, الخاسرون being the khabar of the second, and the nominal clause the khabar of أولئك.

dervis-irab:38-40.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ يَنْتَهُوا يُغْفَرْ لَهُمْ ما قَدْ سَلَفَ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) قل. There is disagreement about the meaning of this lām. The most likely is that it is for conveying (li-l-tablīgh): he was commanded to convey to them the clause quoted by the saying, whether they [the conveyers] transmit it in this wording or in other wording that renders its meaning and content. al-Zamakhsharī chose that it is causal, i.e. say this saying for their sake, namely: إن ينتهوا etc.
al-Zamakhsharī's argument is that if it meant "address them", it would have been said: إن انتهوا يغفر لكم (if you desist, you will be forgiven).
إن is conditional; ينتهوا is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); يغفر, in the passive, is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يغفر; ما is a relative noun, the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause قد سلف is the ṣila (relative clause). (وَإِنْ يَعُودُوا فَقَدْ مَضَتْ سُنَّتُ الْأَوَّلِينَ): the wāw is conjunctive; إن is conditional; يعودوا is the protasis, and what it is attached to is omitted, i.e. to fighting him or to disbelief, and both are meant. فقد: the fāʾ links the apodosis; قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); مضت سنة الأولين is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (وَقاتِلُوهُمْ حَتَّى لا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ وَيَكُونَ الدِّينُ كُلُّهُ لِلَّهِ): conjoined to قل للذين. The command was singular in the first because the address is to the Prophet alone, concerning what falls within the scope of his mission; and the command was plural in the second because the address is to all the believers, to rouse them to war and to fighting their enemy and the stirrers of fitna in general. حتى is a particle of limit and of the genitive; لا is negating; تكون is in the accusative (manṣūb) by an أن implied after حتى; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to قاتلوهم. تكون here is complete (tāmma), and فتنة is its fāʿil. يكون is conjoined to تكون, and here it is defective (nāqiṣa): الدين is its noun, كله is a tawkīd (emphasis), and لله is the khabar (predicate). (فَإِنِ انْتَهَوْا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِما يَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ): the fāʾ is conjunctive; إن is conditional; انتهوا is a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis; the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa); إنّ and its noun, and بصير is its khabar; بما يعملون is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to بصير; the clause يعملون is the ṣila. (وَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ مَوْلاكُمْ نِعْمَ الْمَوْلى وَنِعْمَ النَّصِيرُ): conjoined to what precedes it, and the i'rab is similar. أنّ together with what falls in its scope stands in place of the two objects of اعلموا. نعم is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing praise; المولى is the fāʿil; the one specified for praise (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-madḥ) is omitted, i.e. هو (He); and likewise ونعم النصير.
[Volume Four]
[Continuation of Surat al-Anfāl]

dervis-irab:41-42.t:
* Vocabulary:
(العدوة), with ḍamma on the ʿayn, and kasra and fatḥa are also permissible: the bank of the valley and its edge. It was so named [Translator's note: the source has the misprint «سسيت» for «سميت»] because it prevents (ʿadat) the water and the like that is in the valley from passing beyond it, i.e. it holds it back. In Mukhtār al-Ṣiḥāḥ: العدوة, with ḍamma and kasra on the ʿayn, is the side of the valley and its edge. Abū ʿAmr said: it is the elevated place.
(الدنيا والقصوى): the feminines of الأدنى (nearer) and الأقصى (farther). One of them came with yāʾ and the other with wāw, although both are of the pattern فُعلى from roots with wāw, because the rule (qiyās) is to change the wāw into yāʾ, as in العليا; as for القصوى, it is like العود [Translator's note: so in the source; probably a misprint for القَوَد, a standard example of a form kept on its original pattern] in coming on the original form. القصيا has also occurred, but the use of القصوى is more frequent. Now, the nearer bank is the one adjoining Medina, and the farther is the one adjoining Mecca.
(الرَّكْبُ): in al-Qāmūs: الركب: riders of camels; it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) of راكب, or a plural of it, and they are ten or more; it may also be used for horses. The plural is أركب and ركوب.

* I'rab:
(وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّما غَنِمْتُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ): أنّ together with what falls in its scope stands in place of the two objects of اعلموا. ما is a relative noun, and that is why it is separated (lit. "set apart") in the script from [أنّ]; but its joining is established in the script of some muṣḥafs and its separation in others. It is the noun of أنّ; the clause غنمتم is the ṣila (relative clause); من شيء is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the implied pronoun referring back to the relative noun. The meaning is: whatever you have taken as spoils, being of anything, i.e. whether little or much. (فَأَنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُ وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِي الْقُرْبى وَالْيَتامى وَالْمَساكِينِ وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ): the fāʾ is linking, because of the hint of condition in the relative noun. The hamza of «أنّ» takes fatḥa because it, together with what falls in its scope, is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being: فحكمه أن لله خمسه (its ruling is that a fifth of it is for Allah). The preposition and its genitive noun are the khabar of أنّ placed first, and خمسه is its noun placed after; the implied form is: فإن خمسه لله. أنّ together with what falls in its scope may also be a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being: فحقّ or فواجب أن لله خمسه (then it is due / obligatory that a fifth of it is for Allah). للرسول and what follows it are conjoined to His saying لله. The details of the division will come in the section on benefits. (إِنْ كُنْتُمْ آمَنْتُمْ بِاللَّهِ وَما أَنْزَلْنا عَلى عَبْدِنا يَوْمَ الْفُرْقانِ): إن is conditional; كنتم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being: then know that. The clause آمنتم is the khabar of كنتم; بالله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) آمنتم; ما is conjoined to الله; the clause أنزلنا is the ṣila; على عبدنا is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنزلنا; يوم الفرقان is an adverb also attached to أنزلنا, and what is meant by it is the day of Badr, which separated truth and falsehood. (يَوْمَ الْتَقَى الْجَمْعانِ): the adverb is a badal (substitute) for the first adverb, and the clause التقى الجمعان is annexed to the adverb. (وَاللَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): the wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ and قدير its khabar; على كل شيء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to قدير. (إِذْ أَنْتُمْ بِالْعُدْوَةِ الدُّنْيا وَهُمْ بِالْعُدْوَةِ الْقُصْوى): the adverb is a badal for the first or the second يوم; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ and بالعدوة the khabar, and the clause is annexed to the adverb; الدنيا is a naʿt (adjective) of العدوة; وهم بالعدوة القصوى is conjoined to the preceding one. (وَالرَّكْبُ أَسْفَلَ مِنْكُمْ): the wāw is circumstantial, [the ḥāl being] from the adverbial expression, namely His saying «بالعدوة القصوى»; it may also be conjunctive, joining to «أنتم», because it is the beginning of a division of their circumstances and the circumstances of their enemy. الركب is a mubtadaʾ; أسفل is in the accusative as an adverb, in the position of a nominative as the khabar; more discussion of it will come in the section on benefits. منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أسفل, because it was originally an elative (ism tafḍīl) used in the sense of a naʿt of an omitted place, and put in its place. al-Zamakhsharī has a section explaining the reason for this specification of time and the mention of the positions of the two parties; we will cite it in the section on benefits, because it reaches the summit in probing the secrets of the Mighty Book. (وَلَوْ تَواعَدْتُمْ لَاخْتَلَفْتُمْ فِي الْمِيعادِ): the wāw is conjunctive; لو is conditional, indicating non-occurrence; تواعدتم is the protasis; the lām is linking; اختلفتم is a clause with no grammatical position because it is the apodosis; في الميعاد is attached to اختلفتم. I.e. your disagreeing about the appointed time for going out to battle did not occur because your making an appointment with one another, and informing one another about going out to battle, did not occur; for you might weaken when you learned of their strength and the inaccessibility of their position — which supports al-Zamakhsharī's marvellous section. (وَلكِنْ لِيَقْضِيَ اللَّهُ أَمْراً كانَ مَفْعُولًا): لكن is an inoperative particle of rectification (istidrāk); ليقضي: the lām is causal, and together with its interpreted genitive it is attached to an omitted [verb], i.e. He brought you together without an appointment. الله is the fāʿil (agent); أمرا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause كان مفعولا is a naʿt of أمرا: كان, its latent (mustatir) noun and its khabar. (لِيَهْلِكَ مَنْ هَلَكَ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ): ليهلك may be attached to what ليقضي is attached to, i.e. it is a badal for it; it may also be attached to مفعولا. يهلك is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an أن implied after the causal lām; من is a relative noun, the fāʿil; the clause هلك is the ṣila; عن بينة is a ḥāl.
(وَيَحْيى مَنْ حَيَّ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ): conjoined to the preceding clause. حيّ was originally حيي; the yāʾ was assimilated into the yāʾ. (وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَسَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive; إنّ and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); سميع is the first khabar of إنّ and عليم a second khabar.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «إذ أنتم بالعدوة الدنيا» up to His saying «ويحيا من حي عن بينة» there is the device of istidrāk (rectification). For the Truth, glory be to Him, reported the event that took place with a statement that eloquence made run the course of a proverb. That is: when the Messenger ﷺ was informed by his scouts of the return of the Quraysh caravan from Syria to Mecca along the well-known highway, whose traveller must pass by «Badr», he ordered his Companions to go out, and went out with them seeking the caravan. Allah's promise of one of the two parties had already come to him: either the caravan or the armed force. Abū Sufyān, who was in charge of the caravan, learned that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had set out, so he ordered the caravan to take the coast road, and Abū Sufyān went straight on to Mecca and called Quraysh to arms. They went out to Badr to divert the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from pursuing the caravan, and they came upon him at Badr while he thought that the caravan would pass by Badr. So the encounter took place without an appointment. Allah, glory be to Him, reported the position of the Muslims at Badr and the position of the polytheists there in His saying:
«إذ أنتم بالعدوة الدنيا», i.e. the near one, «وهم بالعدوة القصوى», i.e. the far one, «والركب أسفل منكم», because the coast is in a depression, and Badr is on high ground relative to it. He wished to report that the encounter occurred without an appointment, and turned from the direct wording of the meaning to the wording of irdāf (expressing a meaning through its consequence): He did not say "so they met without an appointment", but said: «ولو تواعدتم لاختلفتم في الميعاد», so that the expression of irdāf would run the course of a proverb, to be more current and more widely known. Had it been limited to this amount, it might have been said: what is the wisdom in Allah depriving His Messenger and the Muslims of this easy booty لأجل منها [Translator's note: so in the source; the phrase appears to be defective, probably for «لأجل ما هو أعظم منها», "for the sake of something greater than it"], namely the conquest of Mecca and the taking of all its people's wealth? For His choosing for them the encounter with the armed force rather than the caravan was so that the defenders of Mecca and its chiefs would be killed, and the Muslims would be able to conquer it — and so it was. The Muslims' wish had been to meet the caravan rather than the armed force, as is shown by His report of them, glory be to Him, in His saying:
«ويودون أن غير ذات الشوكة تكون لكم», meaning the caravan, for ذات الشوكة (the one with the thorn) is the armed force, since الشوكة is weaponry. So they wanted that, and Allah wanted the opposite, because of His knowledge of the outcomes. So He caused the encounter to take place without an appointment for this benefit, and made the report of it run the course of a proverb, for the benefit of that which we have explained. Then He strengthened the evidence of the speech by mentioning the reason for letting that apparent benefit pass, saying with the wording of istidrāk: «ولكن ليقضي الله أمرا كان مفعولا». Then He detailed what He had summarised in the istidrāk with His saying: «لِيَهْلِكَ مَنْ هَلَكَ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ وَيَحْيى مَنْ حَيَّ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ». So the difficulty was made clear, the supposed possibility was removed, and the meaning was set forth in the best of exposition. Thus in these words fourteen kinds of rhetoric are found: concision (ījāz), preparation (tarshīḥ), irdāf, representation (tamthīl), juxtaposition (muqārana), istidrāk, embedding (idmāj), clarification (īḍāḥ), refinement (tahdhīb), giving reasons (taʿlīl), pointed choice (tankīt), equivalence (musāwāt), good arrangement (ḥusn al-nasaq) and good exposition (ḥusn al-bayān).

* Benefits:
1- In this book we have not undertaken to go deeply into scholarly and legal questions except rarely, and only in what has a connection with i'rab or eloquence. The scholars have gone deeply into how the fifth is divided, and we summarise the views of the imams in a way that does not depart from our method.
The division of the fifth according to Abū Ḥanīfa is that in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ it was in five shares: a share for the Messenger of Allah, a share for his kin, and three shares for the orphans, the poor and the wayfarer.
According to al-Shāfiʿī it is divided into five shares: a share for the Messenger of Allah, spent on what he used to spend it on of the interests of the Muslims, such as the equipment of the fighters in weapons, horses and the like; a share for the kin, both their rich and their poor; and the rest for the three groups.
According to Mālik ibn Anas, the matter is left to the independent judgement (ijtihād) of the imam: if he sees fit, he divides it among these; if he sees fit, he gives it to some of them and not others; and if he sees others as more deserving and more important, then to others. There are other views, which may be consulted in the lengthy works.
2- The khabar may be an adverb, as in «والركب أسفل منكم», or a preposition and its genitive noun, as in «الحمد لله». The condition for both is that they be complete (tāmm), as exemplified; so one may not say زيد مكانا [Translator's note: the source has «مكافا», evidently a misprint for «مكانا»] ("Zayd is a place"), nor زيد بك ("Zayd is with you"), because they convey nothing. They are necessarily attached to an omitted word which is the khabar. Its implied form is disputed: it is said to be استقرّ (it settled) or مستقرّ (settled).
Ibn Hishām said in al-Mughnī: "The truth, in my view, is that neither implying it as a noun nor as a verb is preferable, but rather according to the meaning." Ibn Mālik said in al-Khulāṣa:
وأخبروا لظرف أو بحرف جر ... ناوين معنى كائن أو استقر
(Gloss: They have predicated with an adverb or with a preposition, intending the meaning of كائن ("being") or استقر ("settled").)
There are important remarks to which we draw attention:
a- Place may be predicated of nouns of concrete entities and of abstract nouns, as in: زيد خلفك (Zayd is behind you) and الخير أمامك (good is ahead of you).
b- Time may be predicated only of abstract nouns, as in: الصوم اليوم (the fast is today) and السفر غدا (the journey is tomorrow).
c- Time is not predicated of nouns of concrete entities; one does not say: زيد اليوم (Zayd is today). The difference is that events are actions and movements, so every event must have a time specific to it, unlike concrete entities.
d- If something useful is conveyed, it is permissible to predicate time of concrete entities, as when the mubtadaʾ is general and the time is specific, by annexation or description, as in: نحن في شهر كذا (we are in such-and-such a month). نحن is a mubtadaʾ, and it is general because in itself it is fit for every speaker, since no speaker has it to the exclusion of others; في شهر كذا is its khabar, and it is made specific by the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). And: نحن في زمن طيب (we are in a good time), made specific by the description.
e- As for their sayings «الورد في أيار» (the rose is in May), «اليوم خمر» (today is wine) and «الليلة الهلال» (tonight is the new moon), their interpretation is: the coming out of the rose; today is the drinking of wine; tonight is the sighting of the new moon. So the predication is in reality about an abstract noun, not a noun of a concrete entity.
3- It is now time to cite al-Zamakhsharī's section in his exact words; in it this imam rises to the farthest horizon and demonstrates the strength of his observation and the soundness of his thinking. He said:
«If you say: What is the benefit of this specification of time and the mention of the positions of the two parties, and that the caravan was below them? I say: the benefit in it is to report the circumstance that indicates the strength of the enemy's standing and its might, the completeness of its equipment and the preparedness of the means of victory for it, and the weakness of the Muslims' standing and the confusion of their affair; and that their victory in such a circumstance was nothing but a work of Allah, glory be to Him, and a proof that it was a matter made possible only by His might, His power and His dazzling omnipotence. That is because the far bank, where the polytheists made camp, had water and was a passable land, while there was no water on the near bank, and it was soft ground (khabār) in which the feet sank — «i.e. loose» — and one could walk in it only with fatigue and hardship. The caravan was behind the backs of the enemy, along with their great numbers, so protecting it redoubled their zeal and sharpened their resolve in fighting for it. This is why the Arabs used to go out to war with their women and their wealth, so that defending their sanctuaries and jealousy for their womenfolk would rouse them to exert their utmost in fighting, and so that they would not leave behind them anything to which they might be tempted to withdraw. That would unite their hearts, discipline their resolve and settle their souls on not leaving their positions or abandoning their posts, and on exerting the utmost of their valour and the limit of their strength. In it there is also a depiction of what He, glory be to Him, arranged in the matter of the battle of Badr, in order to accomplish a matter that was to be done — the strengthening of His religion and the raising of His word — when He promised the Muslims one of the two parties, vaguely and without specifying it, so that they went out to take the caravan, eager to go out.
[Translator's note: the source does not mark where al-Zamakhsharī's quotation ends; the entry ends here.]

dervis-irab:43-44.t:
* I'rab:
(إِذْ يُرِيكَهُمُ اللَّهُ فِي مَنامِكَ قَلِيلًا): the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [verb], its implied form being اذكر (remember); or it is a second badal (substitute) for يوم الفرقان; or it is attached to سميع عليم, i.e. He knows what is beneficial when He makes them few in your eye. يريكهم is an imperfect verb; the kāf is the first object, the hāʾ the second object; الله is the fāʿil (agent); في منامك is a ḥāl (circumstantial); قليلا is a third object, because رأى of dreaming takes two objects in the accusative without the hamza, and when the hamza enters it, it takes three. (وَلَوْ أَراكَهُمْ كَثِيراً لَفَشِلْتُمْ وَلَتَنازَعْتُمْ فِي الْأَمْرِ): the wāw is conjunctive; لو is conditional; أراكهم is a past verb, the kāf being the first object, the hāʾ the second object, and كثيرا a third object; the lām is linking; فشلتم is a verb and its fāʿil; لتنازعتم is conjoined to لفشلتم; في الأمر is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تنازعتم. (وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ سَلَّمَ إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ): the wāw is conjunctive; لكنّ and its noun, and the clause سلّم is its khabar (predicate); إنه: إنّ and its noun, and عليم is its khabar; بذات الصدور is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to عليم. (وَإِذْ يُرِيكُمُوهُمْ إِذِ الْتَقَيْتُمْ فِي أَعْيُنِكُمْ قَلِيلًا): إذ is a badal for the adverb before it; يريكموهم is an imperfect verb, the kāf being the first object, the mīm the sign of the plural, the wāw for lengthening the mīm, and the hāʾ the second object; إذ is attached to يريكموهم, and the clause التقيتم is annexed to the adverb; في أعينكم is attached to قليلا; قليلا is a ḥāl from the hāʾ, because the seeing here is visual, so with the hamza it takes only two objects. (وَيُقَلِّلُكُمْ فِي أَعْيُنِهِمْ لِيَقْضِيَ اللَّهُ أَمْراً كانَ مَفْعُولًا): conjoined to what preceded; في أعينهم is a ḥāl; ليقضي: the causal lām with its genitive is attached to يقللكم, because it is the reason for [what is] explained. He repeated it because the action explained differs: the action explained the first time is their gathering without an appointment, and the second time the making of the believers few before the clash, then making them many in the eyes of the disbelievers. As for the purpose of making the disbelievers few in the eyes of the believers, it is evident. As for making the believers few in their eyes before the encounter, that was so that they would venture against them with little regard for them, until, when the great number took them by surprise, they would be stunned and awed and utterly confounded. The clause كان مفعولا is a naʿt (adjective) of الأمر.
(وَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الْأُمُورُ): the wāw is conjunctive; إلى الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ترجع; الأمور is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

dervis-irab:45-47.t:
* Vocabulary:
(رِيحُكُمْ): الريح (wind) here means power/fortune (al-dawla). It was likened, in the effectiveness and course of its command, to the wind and its blowing; so it is said: هبت رياح فلان (so-and-so's winds blew), when fortune turned in his favour and his command became effective. Sulayk ibn al-Sulaka said:
يا صاحبيّ ألا لا حيّ بالوادي ... إلا عبيد مقود بين أذواد
أتنظران قليلا ريث غفلتهم ... أم تعدوان فإن الريح للعادي
(Gloss: O my two companions, there is no one alive in the valley but slaves leading [camels] among small herds. Will you wait a little until they are heedless, or will you run [at them]? For the wind belongs to the one who runs.)
The poet borrowed "wind" for power/fortune, by the common element of effectiveness and effective command in each; so it is figurative (majāz). [One says:] إذا هبت رياحك فاغتنمها (when your winds blow, seize the chance); and رجل ساكن الريح (a man of still wind):
dignified. In al-Qāmūs and al-Mukhtār: الريح is used to mean strength, prevailing, mercy, help, and power/fortune.
(البطر) and الأشر, each with two fatḥas: excess in [the enjoyment of] a blessing by failing to give thanks for it and making it a means to what Allah is not pleased with. It is also said: their meaning is boasting of a blessing and meeting it with arrogance and conceit.
(الرئاء): the maṣdar (verbal noun) of راءى, like قاتل قتالا. The original is رياء [Translator's note: so in the source; the original form meant is presumably رِيَايٌ]. The first hamza is a substitute for a yāʾ that is the ʿayn (middle radical) of the word, and the second is a substitute for a yāʾ that is the lām (final radical) of the word, because it occurred ظرفا [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently a misprint for طرفا, "at the end"] after an extra alif.

* I'rab:
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذا لَقِيتُمْ فِئَةً فَاثْبُتُوا): إذا is a particle [Translator's note: so in the source, «حرف»; elsewhere the author calls it an adverb] for future time, putting its protasis in the genitive and being in the accusative by its apodosis; the clause لقيتم is annexed [to it]; فئة is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa); اثبتوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (وَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيراً لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ): اذكروا is conjoined to اثبتوا; it is an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the Name of Majesty is a mafʿūl bihi; كثيرا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) because it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar; it may also be parsed as an adverb, i.e. a great deal of time. لعلكم تفلحون: لعلّ and its noun, and the clause تفلحون is its khabar (predicate). (وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَلا تَنازَعُوا فَتَفْشَلُوا وَتَذْهَبَ رِيحُكُمْ): أطيعوا is conjoined to اذكروا; the Name of Majesty is a mafʿūl bihi and رسوله is conjoined to it; لا is prohibitive; تنازعوا, originally تتنازعوا, is in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا; the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya), because it occurs in the response to a prohibition; تفشلوا is an imperfect in the accusative (manṣūb) by an أن implied after the fāʾ of causation; وتذهب ريحكم is conjoined to فتفشلوا. The wāw [Translator's note: so in the source; the particle meant is presumably the fāʾ] may also be conjunctive, and تفشلوا jussive because it falls under the ruling of the prohibition; and it has been read thus.
(وَاصْبِرُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ): conjoined to what preceded; إنّ and its noun, and the adverb is its khabar. (وَلا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا مِنْ دِيارِهِمْ بَطَراً وَرِئاءَ النَّاسِ): ولا تكونوا is conjoined to what preceded; تكونوا is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, and the wāw is its noun; كالذين: the kāf is a noun meaning مثل (like), its khabar, and الذين is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); or they are a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar of تكونوا. What is meant by them is the people of Mecca when they went out to protect the caravan: Abū Sufyān's messenger came to them while they were at al-Ḥujfa [Translator's note: so in the source; the place is al-Juḥfa], [saying] that they should go back, for their caravan was safe. But Abū Jahl refused and said: "Not until we come to Badr [Translator's note: the source has «بئرا», "a well", evidently a misprint for «بدرا»], drink wine there, have singing-girls play for us, and feed the Arabs around us." That was their arrogance and their showing off. So they reached it, were given the cup of death to drink, and the wailing women wailed over them in place of the singing-girls. بطرا is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); it may also be parsed as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); and likewise رئاء الناس. (وَيَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ بِما يَعْمَلُونَ مُحِيطٌ): the wāw is conjunctive, and the clause يصدون is conjoined to بطرا, i.e. "and barring from the way of Allah". He turned from the nominal to the verbal [form] in the barring only because arrogance and showing off were their habit and custom, unlike the barring, which arose anew for them in the time of prophethood. The wāw is resumptive; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and محيط its khabar; بما يعملون is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to محيط.

dervis-irab:48-49.t:
* Vocabulary:
(نَكَصَ عَلى عَقِبَيْهِ): he went back retreating, walking backwards. The poet said:
ليس النكوص على الأعقاب مكرمة ... إن المكارم إقدام على الأصل
(Gloss: Turning back on one's heels is no noble deed; noble deeds are pressing forward against the spears.)
العقب, with kasra or sukūn on the qāf: the back of the foot; also offspring and the offspring of offspring; the plural is أعقاب. أعقاب الأمور is the ends of affairs. One says: جاء عقبه and بعقبه, i.e. he came after him; رجع على عقبه, i.e. he went back quickly along the road by which he had come; وطئ عقبه, i.e. he walked in his footsteps; سافر على عقب الشهر, i.e. at its end.

* I'rab:
(وَإِذْ زَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطانُ أَعْمالَهُمْ): the adverb إذ is in the accusative by an omitted اذكر (remember); the clause زين is annexed to it; لهم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) زين; الشيطان is the fāʿil (agent) and أعمالهم a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (وَقالَ: لا غالِبَ لَكُمُ الْيَوْمَ مِنَ النَّاسِ): قال is conjoined to زين; لا is the lā of generic negation; غالب is its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa; لكم is its khabar (predicate); من الناس is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in لكم, because it contains the meaning of being settled (istiqrār).
(وَإِنِّي جارٌ لَكُمْ): the wāw conjoins the clause within the scope of the saying, and that is why its hamza takes kasra; إنّ and its noun, and جار is its khabar; لكم is attached to جار, because it means one who gives you protection, help and support. It is said that Satan came to them in the form of Surāqa ibn Mālik, chief of a district of Kināna. (فَلَمَّا تَراءَتِ الْفِئَتانِ نَكَصَ عَلى عَقِبَيْهِ): the fāʾ is conjunctive; لمّا is an adverb meaning حين (when), or a linking [particle]; تراءت الفئتان is a verb and its fāʿil; نكص is conjoined to تراءت [Translator's note: so in the source; نكص is more usually taken as the response of لمّا], and the clause has no grammatical position; على عقبيه is a ḥāl, i.e. fleeing. (وَقالَ: إِنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِنْكُمْ): قال is conjoined to نكص; إنّ, its noun and its khabar; منكم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to بريء; the clause is the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl). (إِنِّي أَرى ما لا تَرَوْنَ): إنّ and its noun, and the clause أرى is its khabar; ما is a mafʿūl bihi; the clause لا ترون is the ṣila (relative clause), and the pronoun referring back is omitted. (إِنِّي أَخافُ اللَّهَ وَاللَّهُ شَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ): إنّ and its noun, and the clause أخاف الله is its khabar; الله is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and شديد العقاب the khabar, and the clause is conjoined to what is within the scope of the saying. (إِذْ يَقُولُ الْمُنافِقُونَ وَالَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ): the adverb is governed by اذكر or by نكص; the clause يقول المنافقون is annexed [to it]; الذين is conjoined to المنافقون; في قلوبهم is a khabar placed first and مرض a mubtadaʾ placed after, and the clause is the ṣila. (غَرَّ هؤُلاءِ دِينُهُمْ): the clause is the object of speech; هؤلاء is the object of غرّ and دينهم its fāʿil. These hypocrites and sick-hearted ones mean that the Muslims were deluded by their religion, and their souls tempted them to face nearly a thousand while they were no more than three hundred and some ten men. So Allah said to them in rebuke: (وَمَنْ يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ): the wāw is resumptive; من is conditional, a mubtadaʾ; يتوكل is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); على الله is attached to يتوكل; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being يغلب (he will prevail); the fāʾ links [what follows as] the reason; فإن الله عزيز حكيم: إنّ, its noun and its two khabars.

dervis-irab:50-54.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَوْ تَرى إِذْ يَتَوَفَّى الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الْمَلائِكَةُ): the wāw is resumptive; ترى is an imperfect verb, and it is visual [seeing]; its agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being أنت (you); the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is omitted, i.e. the disbelievers or their state; إذ is an adverb of ترى, i.e. if you could see the disbelievers, or the state of the disbelievers, when the angels take them in death at Badr. The لو of non-occurrence turns the imperfect verb into a past, just as «إن» turns the past into an imperfect [in meaning]. The clause يتوفى is annexed [to إذ]; الذين is a mafʿūl bihi and الملائكة the fāʿil (agent); the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause). The secret of omitting the apodosis of لو and the mafʿūl bihi has been discussed before, and both are combined here. The implied form of the apodosis is:
"you would have seen something tremendous". (يَضْرِبُونَ وُجُوهَهُمْ وَأَدْبارَهُمْ وَذُوقُوا عَذابَ الْحَرِيقِ): the clause يضربون is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الملائكة or from الذين كفروا, since it contains pronouns referring to both. The agent of يتوفى may also be a pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, since He was mentioned before in His saying ومن يتوكل على الله; in that case الملائكة is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is what follows it, and the clause is a ḥāl from الذين كفروا. ذوقوا is conjoined to يضربون with a verb of saying intended, i.e. "and they say: taste…"; عذاب الحريق is a mafʿūl bihi. (ذلِكَ بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ لَيْسَ بِظَلَّامٍ لِلْعَبِيدِ): ذلك is nominative as a mubtadaʾ and بما قدمت is its khabar; ما is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun) or relative; أيديكم is the fāʿil; وأن الله is conjoined to ما, i.e. that punishment is for two reasons: because of your disbelief and your sins, and because Allah …. The clause ليس is the khabar of أنّ; بظلام: the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition and ظلام is the khabar of ليس by position; للعبيد is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) ظلام. ظلام is an intensive form (ṣīghat mubālagha) conveying attribution (nasab). (كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ): the kāf is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. the way of these is like the way of Pharaoh's people — whether it is a noun or a particle. آل is muḍāf and فرعون muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); الذين is conjoined to آل; من قبلهم is the ṣila of الذين. The clause is resumptive, framed to explain the punishment that befell them because of their disbelief. Ibn ʿAbbās said: the meaning is that Pharaoh's people were certain that Moses, peace and blessings be upon him, was a prophet, yet they denied him; and likewise the state of these: when Muḥammad ﷺ came to them with the truth, they denied him, so Allah sent down His punishment upon them as He sent it down upon Pharaoh's people. (كَفَرُوا بِآياتِ اللَّهِ): the clause كفروا بآيات الله is an explicative of the way of Pharaoh's people; بآيات الله is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to كفروا. (فَأَخَذَهُمُ اللَّهُ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ شَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ): conjoined to كفروا; أخذهم الله is a verb, its mafʿūl bihi and its fāʿil; بذنوبهم is attached to أخذهم, i.e. because of their sins; إنّ and its noun, قوي its first khabar and شديد العقاب its second khabar.
(ذلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ لَمْ يَكُ مُغَيِّراً نِعْمَةً أَنْعَمَها عَلى قَوْمٍ): the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ and بأن الله its khabar; the clause لم يك is the khabar of أنّ; يك is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect in the jussive (majzūm) by لم, the sign of its jussive being the sukūn implied on the nūn that has been dropped for lightness. The special features of kāna will come in the section on benefits. The noun of يك is latent, its implied form being: Allah the Exalted; مغيرا is its khabar; نعمة is the mafʿūl bihi of مغيرا, because it is an active participle; the clause أنعمها is a naʿt (adjective) of نعمة, the hāʾ being a mafʿūl bihi; على قوم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنعمها. (حَتَّى يُغَيِّرُوا ما بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ): حتى is a particle of limit and of the genitive; يغيروا is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an أن implied after حتى; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to مغيرا; ما is a mafʿūl bihi and بأنفسهم is the ṣila of ما. (وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ): conjoined to what precedes it, which is why the hamza of أنّ takes fatḥa, i.e. "and because Allah …"; سميع is the first khabar of أنّ and عليم its second khabar. (كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ): He repeated it for benefits which we summarise as follows:
1- The second statement runs the course of a detailing of the first statement, so the clause is explicative.
2- In the first ayah it was mentioned that they disbelieved in the signs of Allah and rejected them; in the second there is an indication that they denied them as lies, along with their rejecting them and disbelieving in them.
3- The repetition is for emphasis, so the clause is an emphasising one following the first. Its i'rab has been given before in any case.
(كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَهْلَكْناهُمْ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ): the clause is also explicative, as given for the one before it; the clause فأهلكناهم بذنوبهم is conjoined to كذبوا.
(وَأَغْرَقْنا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ): conjoined to what preceded; mentioning the drowning is an explanation of the seizing for sins. (وَكُلٌّ كانُوا ظالِمِينَ): كل is a mubtadaʾ; beginning with it is allowed because of its annexation, the tanwīn standing in for the muḍāf ilayhi, as discussed under the tanwīn of compensation (tanwīn al-ʿiwaḍ), and because of the meaning of generality in it, i.e. all of them, of the drowned Copts and the slain of Quraysh. The clause كانوا ظالمين is the khabar of كل. The pronoun in كانوا and in ظالمين is made plural in consideration of the meaning of كل, because when «كل» is cut off from annexation, it is permissible to consider its wording at times and its meaning at others. Considering the meaning was chosen here only for the sake of the verse-endings (fawāṣil); had only the wording been considered, so that it was said وكل كان ظالما, the verse-endings would not have agreed.

* Rhetoric:
1- Majāz mursal (metonymic trope) in His saying «بما قدمت أيديكم». For this punishment encompassed them only because of their disbelief, and the seat of disbelief is the heart, not the hand, since the hand is not a place of knowledge, so legal responsibility is not directed to it such that punishment could be brought upon it. Rather, the hand here means power, and the relationship is causality, because the hand is the instrument of favour, just as it has been used figuratively in the sense of favour.
2- He turned from ظالم (wrongdoer) to ظلام (great wrongdoer), although the apparent course of speech would require the negation of the lower, since it is more eloquent than negating the higher — for negating the higher does not entail negating the lower, while the reverse [does]. But He turned from that because of العبيد (the servants) [Translator's note: so in the source; the usual explanation refers to the great number of the servants], or because the punishment is so tremendous that, were it not deserved, the one who punished with its like would be ظلام, extreme and enormous in wrongdoing.

* Benefits:
1- The forms فعّال, فاعل and فَعِل in attribution (nisba):
The yāʾ of attribution may be dispensed with by forming the attributed word on the pattern فعّال, with the second letter doubled. That is predominant in trades (ḥiraf, plural of ḥirfa), as بزّاز, with two dotted zāys, for the seller of cloth (bazz); نجار for one whose trade is carpentry; عوّاج for the seller of ivory (ʿāj); and عطّار for the seller of perfume (ʿiṭr). Of the non-predominant use is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
وليس بذي رمح فيطعنني به ... وليس بذي سيف وليس بنبّال
(Gloss: He has no spear to pierce me with, he has no sword, and he is no man of arrows.)
i.e. ذي نبل (possessor of arrows), as is shown by what precedes it; so he used فعّال for something other than a trade. A group of the meticulous scholars interpreted along these lines the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وما ربك بظلام للعبيد», i.e. not a possessor of wrongdoing. What led them to that is that [otherwise] the negation would bear on the intensiveness, and so the root of the action would be affirmed — and Allah the Exalted is far above that. Examples of فعّال are many, yet despite their number Sībawayh said they are not regular (ghayr maqīsa): one does not say دقّاق for the owner of flour (daqīq), nor فكّاه for the owner of fruit (fākiha), nor برّار for the owner of wheat (burr), nor شعّار for the owner of barley (shaʿīr). al-Mubarrad treats this as regular.
- Further, the attributed word is also formed on فاعل, or on فَعِل with fatḥa on the first letter and kasra on the second, in the sense of "possessor of such-and-such". The first is like تامر, i.e. possessor of dates; لابن, possessor of milk; طاعم, possessor of food; and كاس, possessor of clothing. The second is like طعم, possessor of food, and نهر, possessor of daytime. The rajaz poet said:
لست بليلى ولكني نهر ... لا أدلج الليل ولكن أبتكر
(Gloss: I am no man of the night, but a man of the day; I do not travel by night, but set out early in the morning.)
Sībawayh cited it in his Book, i.e. but I am نهاريّ (of the day), i.e. one who works by day.
They differed about the saying of al-Ḥuṭayʾa:
دع المكارم لا ترحل لبغيتها ... واقعد فانك أنت الطاعم الكاسي
(Gloss: Leave noble deeds; do not journey in quest of them; sit down, for you are the one fed and clothed.)
Some said: it is فاعل in the sense of مفعول, i.e. fed and clothed, along the lines of the saying of Allah the Exalted «فهو في عيشة راضية». Others said: it is of the type of attribution, i.e. possessor of food and possessor of clothing. In both cases it is satire, i.e. he has no merit except that he eats and drinks.
2- The special features of kāna:
«كان» is distinguished by several matters:
a- That it may be redundant (zāʾida), under two conditions:
The first: that it be in the past form, because time is determinate in it, unlike the imperfect. Anomalous is the saying of the mother of ʿAqīl ibn Abī Ṭālib, dandling him:
أنت تكون ما جد نبيل ... إذا تهب شمأل بليل
(Gloss: You will be glorious and noble when the cold, moist north wind blows.)
أنت is a mubtadaʾ and ماجد its khabar, and تكون is redundant between the mubtadaʾ and the khabar.
The second: that it be between two things that belong together, which are not a preposition and its genitive noun. What is meant by its redundancy is not that it indicates no meaning at all, but that it was not brought for predication; otherwise it indicates the past. That is why its redundancy is frequent between the ما of wonder and the verb of wonder, since [that verb] has been stripped of indicating the past, as in: ما كان أحسن زيدا (how handsome Zayd was!), كان being redundant between the mubtadaʾ and its khabar. The poet said:
حجبت تحيتها فقلت لصاحبي ... ما كان أكثرها لنا وأقّلها
(Gloss: She withheld her greeting, so I said to my companion: how plentiful it used to be for us, and how scant [now]!)
It may be added between the verb and its nominative, as in the saying of one of them: لم يوجد كان مثلهم (there was not found [anyone] like them), adding كان between the verb and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). There is disagreement about the saying of al-Farazdaq:
فكيف إذا مررت بدار قوم ... وجيران لنا، كانوا، كرام
(Gloss: How then, when I pass by the home of a people, neighbours of ours who were noble?)
Some, among them al-Mubarrad, said: in the verse it is not redundant, but the defective [kāna]; the wāw is its noun and لنا its khabar, and the clause is in the position of a naʿt of جيران, and كرام is a naʿt after a naʿt; so it is parallel to the saying of Allah the Exalted: «هذا كتاب أنزلناه مبارك». Sībawayh and al-Khalīl held that in the verse it is redundant, and their followers have views on explaining how it is joined to the wāw, which may be consulted in the lengthy works.
b- Among them is that it may be omitted while its noun and its khabar remain. That is frequent after the maṣdariyya أن occurring in the position of a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), wherever one action is meant to be explained by another, as in: أمّا أنت منطلقا انطلقت (because you were going, I went). انطلقت is what is explained, and what precedes it is its reason, placed before it. The original is: انطلقت لأن كنت منطلقا; then the causal lām and what follows it, governed by it in the genitive, were put before «انطلقت», so it became: لأن كنت منطلقا انطلقت; then كان was omitted for that reason, and the pronoun which is the noun of كان became detached, so it became: أن أنت منطلقا; then ما was added as compensation for كان, so it became:
أن ما أنت; then the nūn was assimilated into the mīm because of the closeness of their points of articulation, so it became أمّا أنت. On this is the saying of ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās:
أبا خراشة أمّا أنت ذا نفر ... فإن قومي لم تأكلهم الضبع
(Gloss: O Abū Khurāsha, if you boast because you have a band of men — my people have not been devoured by the year of famine.)
i.e. because you were possessed of a band, you boasted; then «فخرت» (you boasted) was omitted, it being what the preposition [governing] أن and what follows it is attached to. أبا خراشة is a vocative. The fāʾ entered on فإن قومي because the second is merited by the first, so it is caused by it and the first is a cause, and so it resembled a condition and its requital.
c- Among them is that it may be omitted together with its noun while the khabar remains. That is frequent after the conditional إن and لو. An example of لو:
لا يأمن الدهر ذو بغي ولو ملكا ... جنوده ضاق عنها السهل والجبل
(Gloss: The oppressor is not safe from time, even if he is a king whose armies are too many for plain and mountain.)
i.e. even if the oppressor were a king with many armies; and the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «التمس ولو خاتما من حديد» (seek, even if only an iron ring), i.e. seek something, even if what you seek is an iron ring.
An example of إن:
قد قيل ما قيل إن صدقا وإن كذبا ... فما اعتذارك من قول إذا قيلا
(Gloss: What was said has been said, whether true or false; so what use is your excuse for a word once it has been said?)
i.e. whether what was said was true or whether what was said was false. And their saying: «الناس مجزيون بأعمالهم إن خيرا فخير وإن شرا فشر» (people are requited for their deeds: if good, then good; if evil, then evil), with the first in the accusative as the khabar of the omitted كان together with its noun, and the second in the nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. if their deed was good, their requital is good, and if their deed was evil, their requital is evil.
d- Among them is that the lām (final radical) of its imperfect, which is the nūn, may be dropped for lightness, in continuous speech, not in pause, on condition that it be in the jussive with sukūn, not joined to an accusative pronoun nor to a vowelless letter, as in: «ولم أك بغيا», and like the ayah we are dealing with.
e- Among them — and in this feature its sisters share with it, except three — is that it may be used as complete (tāmma), i.e. sufficing with its nominative, as in: «وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة», and the saying of Abū Tammām:
قد كان ما خفت أن يكونا ... إنا إلى الله راجعونا
(Gloss: What I feared would happen has happened; we are returning to Allah.)
Its meaning then is "it happened". As for the three that are necessarily defective, they are: فتئ, زال and ليس.

dervis-irab:55-59.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَثْقَفَنَّهُمْ): you come upon them and get the better of them. In al-Miṣbāḥ: ثقفت الشيء ثقفا, of the pattern of تعب: I took it; ثقفت الرجل في الحرب: I caught up with the man in war; ثقفته: I overcame him; ثقفت الحديث: I understood the speech quickly; and the agent [noun] is ثقيف.
(فَانْبِذْ): then throw back the covenant to them. النبذ is throwing away; here it is a majāz (figurative usage) for informing them that they have no covenant after today. The covenant is likened to a thing that is thrown away for lack of desire for it, and throwing is attributed to it as an imaginary attribution (takhyīl). Its object is omitted, i.e. their covenant. More of this important discussion will come in the section on rhetoric.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّ شَرَّ الدَّوَابِّ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): إنّ and its noun; الدواب is annexed to شر (muḍāf ilayhi); عند الله is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); الذين is the khabar (predicate) of إنّ and the clause كفروا is the ṣila (relative clause). The whole clause is resumptive, introduced after the account of the states of those of the worst disbelievers who were destroyed, in order to begin explaining the states of those of them who remained and detailing the rulings concerning them.
(فَهُمْ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (revealing an omitted condition); هم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the clause لا يؤمنون is the khabar, i.e. no belief is to be expected from them after they persisted in disbelief and stubbornly continued in it. (الَّذِينَ عاهَدْتَ مِنْهُمْ): a badal (substitute) for الذين كفروا, so its position is nominative, i.e. those of the disbelievers with whom you made a covenant. He made them the worst of creatures because the worst of people are the disbelievers, the worst of the disbelievers are those of them who persist, and the worst of those who persist are those who broke covenants. The clause عاهدت is the ṣila and منهم is a ḥāl. (ثُمَّ يَنْقُضُونَ عَهْدَهُمْ فِي كُلِّ مَرَّةٍ وَهُمْ لا يَتَّقُونَ): ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; عهدهم is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); في كل مرة is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ينقضون; the wāw is conjunctive; هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا يتقون the khabar. (فَإِمَّا تَثْقَفَنَّهُمْ فِي الْحَرْبِ): the fāʾ is linking, because of the resemblance of the mubtadaʾ to a condition, since the relative noun has a hint of it; إن is conditional and ما redundant (zāʾida), the nūn being assimilated into the mīm; تثقفنهم is an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy emphatic nūn, and it is in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the hāʾ is a mafʿūl bihi; في الحرب is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تثقفنهم. (فَشَرِّدْ بِهِمْ مَنْ خَلْفَهُمْ): the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ (rābiṭa); شرد is an imperative verb; بهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to شرد, the bāʾ having a causal sense, i.e. because of your making an example of them; من is the mafʿūl bihi of شرد, and خلفهم is an adverb attached to an omitted ṣila. The meaning is: when you get the better of these disbelievers who broke the covenant, inflict on them kinds of exemplary punishment by which you scatter the gathering of everyone who breaks a covenant and violates a pledge of protection, so that those behind them fear you. (لَعَلَّهُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ): لعلّ and its noun, and the clause يذكرون is its khabar, i.e. perhaps they will take warning from them. (وَإِمَّا تَخافَنَّ مِنْ قَوْمٍ خِيانَةً): the wāw is conjunctive; إن is conditional, assimilated with the redundant ما; تخافن is the protasis, but it is indeclinable because it is joined to the heavy emphatic nūn; the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being أنت (you); من قوم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تخافن; خيانة is a mafʿūl bihi.
(فَانْبِذْ إِلَيْهِمْ عَلى سَواءٍ): the fāʾ is linking; انبذ is an imperative verb; إليهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to انبذ; على سواء is in the position of a ḥāl from both the agent and the object together, i.e. the agent of the verb, which is the pronoun of the Prophet, and its object, which is what is governed in the genitive by إلى; i.e. while they are equal in knowing of the dissolution of the covenant. More discussion will come of this ayah of marvellous style. (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الْخائِنِينَ): إنّ and its noun, and the clause لا يحب الخائنين is its khabar. The clause gives the reason for the command to throw back [the covenant] and for the prohibition of opening hostilities [abruptly], indicated by the ḥāl, by way of resumption. (وَلا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَبَقُوا إِنَّهُمْ لا يُعْجِزُونَ): the wāw is conjunctive; لا is prohibitive; يحسبن is an indeclinable imperfect in the position of a jussive by the prohibitive لا; الذين كفروا is the fāʿil (agent); the first object is omitted, i.e. themselves; the clause سبقوا is the second object of يحسبن, i.e. that they have escaped His punishment and been saved from it; إنّ and its noun, and the clause لا يعجزون is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
The device of ishāra (allusive brevity):
In the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وإما تخافن من قوم خيانة فانبذ إليهم على سواء» there is a device called «the device of ishāra (pointing)». Some include it under ījāz (concision), since it branches off from it, but Qudāma made it a branch of the harmony of wording with meaning, and explained it, saying: it is that a small amount of wording indicates a great deal of meaning, so that the indication of the wording to the meaning is like pointing with the hand, which points with a single movement to many things which, if expressed by their names, would need a long expression and many words. The difference between it and ījāz is that ījāz is by means of the words coined for the meaning, whereas the words of ishāra are an indicative glance; so the indication of the wording in ījāz is a correspondence indication (dalālat muṭābaqa), while the indication of the wording in ishāra is either an indication by inclusion (dalālat taḍammun) or by entailment (dalālat iltizām). So the saying of Allah the Exalted:
«فانبذ إليهم على سواء» points to the command to fight by throwing back the covenant, as they threw back your covenant, together with the justice indicated by the command to equality in the action. If you add to that what the word خيانة (betrayal) points to — the existence of a previous treaty — it becomes clear to you what these hidden pointers contain of indications that are like a spell of magic.
The scholars have elaborated variously in building the ruling of the ayah. They said: if signs of breaking the covenant appear from those polytheists with whom the imam has made a truce, by an evident and widely known matter, the imam has no need to throw back the covenant and inform them of war. If betrayals appear through signs that glimmer and become clear to him without a widely known matter, then he must throw back [the covenant] to them and inform them of war. But if the breaking of the covenant appears decisively, the imam has no need to throw back the covenant; rather he does as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did with the people of Mecca when they broke the covenant by killing [men of] Khuzāʿa, who were under the protection of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: they were taken by surprise by nothing other than his army at Marr al-Ẓahrān, which is four farsakhs from Mecca.

The device of ishāra in poetry:
As for the device of ishāra in poetry, it is very widespread in our Arabic poetry. Among its most charming instances is the saying of Bahāʾ al-Dīn Zuhayr:
عفا الله عنكم أين ذاك التودّد؟ ... وأين جميل منكم كنت أعهد؟
بما بيننا لا تنقضوا العهد بيننا ... فيسمع واش أو يقول مفند
(Gloss: May Allah pardon you — where is that affection? Where is the kindness from you I used to know? By what is between us, do not break the pact between us, lest a slanderer hear or a censurer speak.)
With ما he pointed to countless motives of love and stirrings of longing. And beautiful is the saying of Abū al-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī:
لعينيك ما يلقى الفؤاد وما لقي ... وللحب ما لم يبق مني وما بقي
(Gloss: For your eyes is what the heart meets and has met; and to love belongs what has not remained of me and what has remained.)
With the first ما and the second ما he pointed to what is not hidden of the passion his heart meets in what lies ahead and what it met before that in what has passed, and of the scars love has made in him — both what sickness has not left of him, of what it has consumed, and what has remained of him, of what it has emaciated and wasted. And Abū Firās has, in ishāra:
وما لك لا تلقى بمهجتك القنا ... وأنت من القوم الذين هم هم
(Gloss: Why do you not meet the spears with your very soul, when you are of the people who are — who they are?)
And how marvellous is the saying of Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī:
منك الصدود ومني بالصّدود رضا ... من ذا عليّ بهذا في هواك قضى
بي منك ما لو بعين الشمس ما طلعت ... من الكآبة أو بالبرق ما ومضا
(Gloss: From you comes aversion, and from me contentment with aversion; who decreed this against me in loving you? I bear from you what, were it in the eye of the sun, it would not rise for grief, or in the lightning, it would not flash.)
As for Khālid al-Kātib, he reached the utmost beauty with his saying:
رقدت ولم ترث للساهر ... وليل المحب بلا آخر
ولم تدر بعد ذهاب الرقا ... د ما فعل الدمع بالناظر
(Gloss: You slept and had no pity for the sleepless one, while the lover's night has no end; and you do not know, after sleep has gone, what tears have done to the eye.)

dervis-irab:1-4.t:
* Vocabulary:
(الْأَنْفالِ): plural of nafl, with fatḥa on the nūn and the fāʾ, like faras and afrās; what is meant by it is the spoils. Nafl is the addition and the booty. From it comes the saying of Labīd:
إنّ تقوى ربّنا خير نفل ... وبإذن الله ريثي وعجل
(The fear of our Lord is the best booty, and by Allah's leave are my slowness and my haste.)
