Labīd likened the reward that Allah promised His servants for fear of Him to the nafl, which is what the Imam sets aside for the fighter as an incitement to plunge into war; so he borrowed «النفل» for it by way of explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), and predicated it of «التقوى» because it is its cause. It is also permissible that nafl be borrowed for fear of Allah on the basis of the common element of benefit. «ريثي» is my slowness, and «عجل» is that is, my haste, the yāʾ being dropped for the metre of the verse. In al-Miṣbāḥ: al-nafl is booty, and the plural is anfāl, like sabab and asbāb; and nafl with sukūn on the fāʾ is the same.
(وَجِلَتْ): wajila with kasra in the past, yawjalu with fatḥa in the imperfect; there is another dialect: wajala with fatḥa on the jīm in the past and kasra in the imperfect, in which the wāw is dropped, like waʿada yaʿidu.

* I'rab:
(يَسْئَلُونَكَ عَنِ الْأَنْفالِ قُلِ الْأَنْفالُ لِلَّهِ وَالرَّسُولِ): Resumptive speech, put forward to establish the legislation of booty in jihad. «يسألونك» is an imperfect verb, agent and direct object; the agent pronoun refers to those who asked this question, among those who were present at the battle of Badr. The verb «سأل» is sometimes used because of a meaning required in the one asked, in which case it is made to govern the second [object] with «عن», as in this verse; and sometimes because of a requirement for goods or money, in which case it governs two objects, as in «سألت زيدا مالا» ("I asked Zayd for money"). «عن الأنفال» is attached to «يسألونك» as preceded; «قل» is an imperative verb; «الأنفال» is a subject (mubtadaʾ), «لله» is its predicate (khabar), and the nominal clause is in the position of an accusative as the maqūl al-qawl (what is said); «الرسول» is conjoined to «الله». (فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَصْلِحُوا ذاتَ بَيْنِكُمْ وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ): The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the eloquent fāʾ); «اتقوا» is an imperative verb and agent; the word of majesty is a direct object; «أصلحوا» is conjoined to «اتقوا»; «ذات بينكم» is a direct object. The meaning of «ذات بينكم» is: the states that are between you, so that they become states of familiarity, love and agreement. Al-bayn here is in the sense of connection, and it is also applied to separation; it is one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād). «إن» is conditional; «كنتم» is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the tāʾ is its noun and «مؤمنين» its predicate; the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. (إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ إِذا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ): «إنما» consists of a restraining and a restrained element (kāffa and makfūfa); «المؤمنون» is a subject; the clause is resumptive, put forward to make clear whom He meant by the believers, by mentioning their majestic attributes that entail the three qualities mentioned next; «الذين» is the predicate; «إذا» is an adverbial (ẓarf) for what is future, containing the meaning of condition; the clause «ذكر الله» is in the position of a genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «الله» is a deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil); the clause «وجلت قلوبهم» has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (وَإِذا تُلِيَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ آياتُهُ زادَتْهُمْ إِيماناً): Conjoined to the first attribute; the clause «زادتهم» has no grammatical position; «إيمانا» is a second direct object or a tamyīz (specification). (وَعَلى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ): A third attribute, falling within the scope of the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; «على ربهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يتوكلون», and the fronting indicates restriction, that is: on Him and not on anyone else. (الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْناهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ): He followed the three preceding attributes — which are acts of the hearts, namely awe, sincerity and trust in Allah — with two attributes from the acts of the limbs, namely establishing prayer and giving charity. The parsing of their like has preceded. (أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ حَقًّا): The demonstrative noun is a subject; «هم» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) or a second predicate; «المؤمنون» is a predicate in any case; the clause is the predicate of the demonstrative noun; the clause is resumptive; «حقا» is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), that is: "they are the believers with true belief"; it is also permissible that it be a maṣdar confirming the content of the sentence, as in your saying: «هو عبد الله حقا» ("he is the servant of Allah, truly"). (لَهُمْ دَرَجاتٌ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ وَرِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ): «لهم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted fronted predicate; «درجات» is a postponed subject; «عند ربهم» is an adverbial attached to «درجات» because it is in the sense of "rewards", or attached to an omitted adjective of «درجات» because it is indefinite; «مغفرة» and «رزق كريم» are conjoined to «درجات».

* Benefits:
History relates that disagreement occurred among the Muslims over the spoils of Badr and their division, so they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: How shall we divide them? And who has the judgement in dividing them? The Emigrants or the Helpers? Or all of them? They were told: They belong to the Messenger, and he alone has the judgement in them, judging as he wishes; no one else has any judgement in them. It was also said: he had stipulated that whoever distinguished himself on that day would be given an extra share. Their young men rushed forward until they had killed seventy and taken seventy captive; and when Allah made the victory easy, they disagreed among themselves and quarrelled. The young men said: We are the fighters. The elders, the notables who had been at the standards, said: We were your support, and a company to which you could retreat if you were routed. They said to the Messenger of Allah: The spoil is little and the people many; if you give these what you stipulated for them, you will deprive your Companions. So it was revealed.

The story of Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ:
On the authority of Saʿīd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ [Translator's note: the Arabic prints «سعيد»; the narration is that of Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, as the heading of this section also says]: "My brother ʿUmayr was killed on the day of Badr, so I killed Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ in retaliation and took his sword. It pleased me, so I brought it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: Allah has healed my breast of the polytheists, so give me this sword. He said: This is neither mine nor yours; throw it into the store, meaning the seized property. So I threw it, with a feeling in me that none knows but Allah the Exalted, from the killing of my brother and the taking of my spoil. I had gone only a little way when the Messenger of Allah came to me, for Sūrat al-Anfāl had been revealed, and said: Saʿd, you asked me for the sword and it was not mine, and now it has become mine; go and take it."

The narration of ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit:
On the authority of ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit: "It was revealed about us, the company of the people of Badr, when we disagreed about the booty and our characters turned bad over it. So Allah took it away from our hands and made it for His Messenger, who divided it among the Muslims equally. In that was fear of Allah, obedience to His Messenger, and the setting right of what is between them."

* Vocabulary:
(الشَّوْكَةِ): The word shawka has many meanings; here it is in the sense of might, strength and weaponry, and sharpness, given that all its meanings return to the meaning of superiority, prominence and dominance. Among its meanings are the scorpion's sting; a redness that rises on the body; and harming the enemy. It is said: «لا تشوكك مني شوكة», that is, no harm will reach you from me.
And the weaver's shawka: the tool with which the warp and weft are levelled. It is said: «شاكت إصبعه شوكة» (a thorn pricked his finger); «شوّكت النخلة» (the palm put forth its thorns); «شوّكت الحائط» (I put thorns on the wall). Figuratively: «شوّك الزرع» and «زرع مشوّك» when its first shoots come out; and «شوّك ثدي الجارية وتشوّك» when it begins to emerge.
[The poet] said:
أحببت هذي قديما وهي ماشية ... وما تشوّك ثدياها وما نهدا
(I loved this one long ago, when she was a walking girl, before her breasts had begun to show or swell.)
When we survey the root shīn-wāw-fāʾ-ʿayn of the word, we find in it a marvellous property, as though it had been set specifically for the meanings of prominence, effect, elevation and superiority. Al-shawb is mixing a thing with another so that it affects it; it is said «شاب العسل بالماء» (he mixed the honey with water), and "as though her saliva were wine mixed with honey". They have al-mashājib and al-mashāwib, which are baskets and chests made of palm leaves; «شوّرت به فتشوّر» ; and from it was said «أبدى الله شوارك» that is, your private parts; and in the hadith of al-Zabbāʾ: «أشوار عروس ترى؟» ("Do you see a bride's trappings?"). This is among the wonders of our noble Arabic language, so understand and ponder.

* I'rab:
(كَما أَخْرَجَكَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَيْتِكَ بِالْحَقِّ): «كما»: it is permissible that the kāf be in the sense of «مثل» (like), its position being nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, its implied form being: "this state is like the state of your being brought out"; and it is permissible that it be a preposition, the position of the preposition and its genitive noun being nominative as preceded. The meaning is: their state in disliking what you saw of giving the fighters extra shares is like their state in disliking your going out to war. It is also permissible that its position be accusative as an adjective of the maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb implied in His saying «الأنفال لله والرسول», that is: the spoils are settled for Allah and the Messenger and established, despite their dislike, with an establishment like the establishment of your Lord's bringing you out of your house while they disliked it. The early parsers expanded greatly on the implied forms and interpretations, and some of them brought them to twenty aspects, but they do not go beyond what we have mentioned. «من بيتك» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «أخرج»; «بالحق» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: accompanied by the truth, wisdom and right from which there is no turning aside. In the section on Benefits there will come the mention of some historical events that clarify this meaning and parsing. (وَإِنَّ فَرِيقاً مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ لَكارِهُونَ): The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); «إن» and its noun; «من المؤمنين» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «كارهون» is the predicate of «إن», and the clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl from the kāf in «أخرجك», that is: He brought you out while they disliked it. (يُجادِلُونَكَ فِي الْحَقِّ بَعْدَ ما تَبَيَّنَ): The clause is resumptive, put forward to report their state of disputing; it is also permissible that it be a second ḥāl from the kāf, that is: He brought you out while they were disputing with you, or from the pronoun in «كارهون», that is: "disliking it while disputing". «في الحق» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يجادلونك»; «بعد» is a temporal adverbial attached to «يجادلونك»; «ما» is a maṣdar particle, and it and what falls within its scope are a maṣdar annexed to the adverbial, that is: after its becoming clear and his going out; and this is uglier than disputing about a thing before it becomes clear. (كَأَنَّما يُساقُونَ إِلَى الْمَوْتِ وَهُمْ يَنْظُرُونَ): The clause is circumstantial from the pronoun in «لكارهون», that is: while they are likened to those who are driven with harshness and humiliation to be killed. «كأنما» consists of a restraining and a restrained element; «يساقون» is a passive imperfect verb and the wāw is the deputy agent; «إلى الموت» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يساقون»; the wāw is circumstantial, and «وهم ينظرون» is a clause in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl. (وَإِذْ يَعِدُكُمُ اللَّهُ إِحْدَى الطَّائِفَتَيْنِ): The wāw is a conjunction; «إذ» is an adverbial attached to an omitted verb, that is «واذكر إذ» ("and remember when"); the clause «يعدكم الله» is in the position of a genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi; «إحدى الطائفتين» is a direct object; an omitted [word] must be implied, that is: "victory over one of the two parties"; the two parties are the caravan and the army. (أَنَّها لَكُمْ وَتَوَدُّونَ أَنَّ غَيْرَ ذاتِ الشَّوْكَةِ تَكُونُ لَكُمْ): «أن» and its noun; «لكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted predicate; «أن» and what falls within its scope are a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) for «إحدى الطائفتين». «وتودون»: the wāw is circumstantial or a conjunction; «تودون» is an imperfect verb, nominative, its sign being the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; «أن» and what falls within its scope are the object of «تودون»; the clause «تكون» is the predicate of «أن»; «لكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun [attached to «تكون»]: the caravan is for you, because it is the party that has no might, and you do not want the other party. [Translator's note: the Arabic text of this phrase reads «ولكم جار ومجرور لكم العير ...», which is garbled; I have translated it as it stands, with the likely sense given.] (وَيُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُحِقَّ الْحَقَّ بِكَلِماتِهِ وَيَقْطَعَ دابِرَ الْكافِرِينَ): The wāw is a conjunction; «يريد الله» is a verb and agent; «أن» is a maṣdar particle, and it and what falls within its scope are the object of «يريد»; «بكلماته» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «يحق». «ويقطع دابر الكافرين» is a conjoined clause; cutting off the rear is an expression for extermination. (لِيُحِقَّ الْحَقَّ وَيُبْطِلَ الْباطِلَ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْمُجْرِمُونَ): The lām is for justification; «يحق» is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied «أن»; the lām and what falls within its scope are attached to an omitted [verb], its implied form being "He did that so that He might establish the truth and nullify falsehood". This is not a repetition of what precedes, because the first is particular and the second general: what is meant by the first is the confirmation of what He promised in this event of victory and triumph, and what is meant by the second is the strengthening and support of the religion and the manifestation and establishment of the Sharia.
(إِذْ تَسْتَغِيثُونَ رَبَّكُمْ): The adverbial is attached to an omitted [verb], that is: "and remember"; it is also permissible that it be attached to «يحق». He expressed it with «الحق» [Translator's note: the Arabic text reads «وعبّر بالحق»; the sense required here is expression by the imperfect, i.e. «بالمضارع»] in narrating the past state; therefore «فاستجاب لكم» was conjoined to it in the past form. (فَاسْتَجابَ لَكُمْ أَنِّي مُمِدُّكُمْ بِأَلْفٍ مِنَ الْمَلائِكَةِ مُرْدِفِينَ): The fāʾ is a conjunction, as preceded; «لكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «استجاب»; «أن» and what falls within its scope are in the position of an accusative by removal of the preposition (nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), that is: "[He responded] that I am going to reinforce you", and the preposition and its genitive noun are also attached to «استجاب»; «ممدكم» is the predicate of «أن»; «بألف» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to «ممدكم»; «من الملائكة» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted adjective of «ألف»; «مردفين» is a second adjective, and the object of «مردفين» is omitted because it is an active participle, that is: "their likes", that is: following one another, or following one another's [ranks].

What does history say?
The caravan of Quraysh came from Syria with great merchandise and with forty riders, among them Abū Sufyān, ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ and ʿAmr ibn Hishām. Jibrīl informed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who informed the Muslims, and they liked the idea of meeting the caravan because of the abundance of good and the fewness of the people. When they set out, the news of their departure reached the people of Mecca, and Abū Jahl called out from above the Kaaba: People of Mecca, to safety, to safety, on every hard and easy mount; your caravan is your wealth; if Muḥammad takes it you will never prosper afterwards. Then Abū Jahl went out with all the people of Mecca, and they are the «النفير» (the army) in the proverb: «لا في العير ولا في النفير» ("neither among the caravan nor among the army"). It was said to him: The caravan has taken the coastal road and escaped, so return with the people to Mecca. He said: No, by Allah, that will never be, until we slaughter camels and drink wine and set up singing girls and instruments at Badr, so that the Arabs hear of our going out, and that Muḥammad did not take the caravan and that we have made him bite [his hand]. So he went on with them to Badr, and Badr is a water at which the Arabs used to gather their camels one day a year. Then Jibrīl came down and said: Muḥammad, Allah has promised you one of the two parties: either the caravan or Quraysh. The Prophet consulted his Companions and said: What do you say? The people have set out from Mecca on every hard and easy mount; do you prefer the caravan or the army? They said: Rather the caravan is dearer to us than meeting the enemy. The face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed, then he went back to them and said: The caravan has passed along the sea coast, and this is Abū Jahl who has come. They said: Messenger of Allah, take the caravan and leave the enemy. At the Prophet's anger, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar stood and spoke well; then Saʿd ibn ʿUbāda stood and said: Look to your command, for by Allah, if you took us to ʿAdan we would go, and no man would lag behind. Then al-Miqdād said: Messenger of Allah, go on to what Allah commanded you, for we are with you; we shall not say to you what the Children of Israel said to Moses: «اذهب أنت وربك فقاتلا إنا هاهنا قاعدون» ("Go, you and your Lord, and fight; we are staying here"), but go, you and your Lord, and fight, for we are fighting with you both as long as an eye of ours blinks. The Messenger of Allah laughed, then said: Advise me, people, meaning the Helpers, because they had said to him when they pledged allegiance to him at al-ʿAqaba: We are free of your protection until you reach our homes, and when you reach us you are under our protection; we shall defend you as we defend our fathers and our women. So the Prophet ﷺ feared that the Helpers would not see themselves obliged to support him except against an enemy who attacked him in Medina. Saʿd ibn Muʿādh stood and said: It is as though you mean us, Messenger of Allah. He said: Indeed. He said: We have believed in you and declared you true, and testified that what you brought is the truth, and we have given you our covenants and pledges on that to hear and obey, so go on, Messenger of Allah, to what you wish; for by Him who sent you with the truth, if you were to take us to this sea and plunge into it, we would plunge into it with you and not one man of us would lag behind; we do not dislike that you meet our enemy with us; we are steadfast in war, true in meeting, and perhaps Allah will show you from us what will delight your eye, so march with us in the blessing of Allah. The Messenger of Allah rejoiced, then said: March in the blessing of Allah and be glad, for Allah has promised me one of the two parties; by Allah, it is as though I now see the places where the people will fall. We have lengthened the quotation because of the importance and eloquence of this passage.
A useful summary of the statements of the parsers on «كما»:
They disagreed on fifteen opinions:
1- That the «kāf» is in the sense of the wāw of oath, and «ما» is in the sense of «الذي» applying to one possessing knowledge, namely Allah, and the answer to the oath is «يجادلونك». Said by Abū ʿUbayda [Translator's note: the Arabic prints «عببيدة», a misprint].
2- That the kāf is in the sense of «إذا» and «ما» is redundant (zāʾida), and the implied form is: "Remember when He brought you out".
3- That the kāf is in the sense of «على» and «ما» in the sense of «الذي».
4- ʿIkrima said: The implied form is: "And obey Allah and His Messenger if you are believers, as His bringing you out in obedience is good for you, so was your bringing out good for them."
5- Al-Kisāʾī said: As your Lord brought you out of your house despite the dislike of a party of them, so they dispute with you about fighting the unbelievers of Mecca, and wish for the one without might, after it had become clear to them that you do only what you were commanded, not what they wish.
6- Al-Farrāʾ said: Go on with your command about the spoils and give extra shares to whom you wish, even if they dislike it, as your Lord brought you out.
7- Al-Akhfash said: The kāf is an adjective of «حقا», and the implied form is: "They are the believers truly, as...".
8- That the kāf is in the position of a nominative, and the implied form is: "As your Lord brought you out, so fear Allah", as though it were a subject and a predicate.
9- Al-Zajjāj said: The kāf is in the position of an accusative, and the implied form is: "The spoils are established for Allah, an establishment like your Lord's bringing you out."
10- That the kāf is in the position of a nominative, and the implied form is: "They have ranks with their Lord, and forgiveness and a generous provision, and this is a true promise, like your Lord's bringing you out."
11- That the kāf is also in the position of a nominative, and the meaning is: "And set right what is between you; that is better for you, as your Lord brought you out", so the kāf is an adjective of the predicate of an omitted subject.
12- That He likened the dislike of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for his going out of Medina, when they were certain that Quraysh had set out to defend Abū Sufyān and protect others, to their dislike of having the booty taken from their hands and made for the Messenger or given as extra shares from it. This opinion was taken by al-Zamakhsharī and he approved it, saying: "The kāf is nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, its implied form being: this state is like the state of your being brought out."
13- That your division of the booty is right, as your going out was right.
14- That the comparison occurs between two bringings out, that is: your Lord's bringing you out of your house — which is Mecca — while you disliked your going out, and the outcome of that was good, victory and triumph, is like your Lord's bringing you out of Medina while some of the believers disliked it, which will be followed by that victory and triumph.
15- The kāf is for comparison by way of figurative speech, like the saying of someone to his servant: "As I sent you to my enemies and they considered you weak, and you asked for reinforcement and I reinforced you and strengthened you, take them now and punish them thus; and as I clothed you and provided for you, do such and such; and as I did good to you, thank me for it."
It is clear that the outcome of these aspects is one, so ponder, and Allah protect you.

* Rhetoric:
1- The representational similes (tashbīhāt tamthīliyya) occurring in the verses we have pointed out during the parsing, because of their close connection with it.
2- Generality and particularity in His saying «ليحق الحق ويبطل الباطل» after His saying «يريد الله أن يحق الحق بكلماته». The precise distinction between the two statements is that in the first the will is mentioned as unrestricted, not bound to the particular event, as though it were said: "You wish that the one without might be yours, and it is Allah's way, Exalted is He, to will the establishment of the truth and the eradication of unbelief in general; and because He willed to establish the truth and nullify falsehood, He gave you the one with might." So between the two statements there are generality and particularity, and unrestrictedness and restriction, and it is not hidden how much emphasis there is in this for the meaning, by mentioning it in two ways: unrestrictedly and restrictedly.
